A trio of new Hulu shows to unwind with now that the week is nearly done

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We’re well into November now, and as the nights darken and become ever more bitter, I need the comforting warmth of the best streaming services like Hulu to get me through this chilly time of year. The three shows I’ve picked out for your streaming pleasure will hopefully keep the winter blues at bay.

My first choice is a new reality show. If you’ve ever wondered what “The Traitors” would look like if Janice Soprano was trying to whack everyone as a pretend mob boss as her wannabe celeb gangsters all vie for $250,000, that’s your weekend plans sorted.

Next up is the new Korean melodrama. I don't normally go in for this genre, but the hook is too good to resist here. Two very different students tentatively start a relationship, with the killer twist being that most of the action is set in a robotics lab. Who says love can’t bloom when you’re building the next T-1000?

Lastly, there’s the second season of the brilliant “The Lowdown”. Ethan Hawke’s bumbling journalist returns to unravel a conspiracy theory regarding Tulsa’s prison system. The big new addition this year? That would be Tommy Lee Jones playing Hawke’s charismatic conman poppa.

Here are three new shows you should definitely add to your Hulu watchlist this weekend. Just don’t forget to turn the heating on.

What is it about? A high-stakes reality show that’s basically “The Traitors”... y’know, if you swapped out Claudia Winkleman’s iconic fringe for a bunch of ‘celebs’ who are tasked to act like wiseguys. Honestly, I’ve not seen a single one of these ‘famous’ folk in my life before, except host Parker Posey and The Sopranos’ Aida Turturro. Anyhoo, the premise is still fun. With the celebs placed in a luxurious Italian villa, they vye for $250,000 by taking part in games lifted straight from mob movies. A new Don gets picked every week, and it’s up to them if their fellow gangster wannabes get paid or get slayed.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Why you should watch it: It’s basically a trashy version of “The Traitors” with a lot more pasta and mob movie-inspired tasks. Turn off your brain, mentally rewatch “Goodfellas” if you’re getting bored and just enjoy all that gorgeous Italian scenery. If nothing else, it’s great to see Janet Soprano back on TV.

What is it about? You know what more romantic dramas really need? Robots, baby! Set in a university robotics lab, love starts to spark between troubled PhD candidate Min-Jae (Choo Young Woo) and free spirit You-jin (Kim So-hyun), who has just transferred in from a clothing and textiles course. Why is Min-Jae so down in the dumps? Before becoming a student of science, he was a professional swimmer whose career ended when he lost his leg. From pro paddler to making robots. That’s quite the career change. Anyway, You-jin eventually gets Min-Jae to open up in this classy Korean melodrama.

Why you should watch it: I’m not usually one for melodramas, but the hook of “Between Steps” is so damn sweet. A couple meets while making things that are basically going to become Terminators in the next few years. Before Arnie destroys their entire lab, just enjoy this sweet drama that really is beautifully shot.

Why you should watch it: Your favorite Tulsa-based ‘truthstorian’ is back in season two of this excellent neo-noir comedy crime drama. All should be well for our freelance journalist Lee Raybon (Ethan Hawke), but the poor guy just can’t seem to get out of his own way. Traumatized from the events of the first season, where he exposed the crooked Washbergs, Lee ends up making an inebriated speech while receiving a journalistic award, quickly disgracing himself. Despite his tattered reputation, Raybon ends up getting drawn into a conspiracy theory centering around local penal corruption. Oh, and his estranged dad also turns up out of the blue.

Why you should watch it: The script is once again excellent in this left-field crime-centric comedy. Hawke is in his usual stellar form, while the addition of his pop Lee Raybon Snr (Tommy Lee Jones) adds a lot. Playing a former Vietnam vet/turned conman with dementia, the pair’s scenes are must-watch.

#3204. Bessent says anyone at Nvidia should be held accountable for chip leakage

The Treasury Secretary told CNBC that four departments wanted Megaspeed blacklisted for months. The decision sits with Howard Lutnick’s Commerce Department, which has not acted.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent at a White House press briefing in Washington on 28 May 2026

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the Nvidia scandal should be about AI chips reaching China, not Jensen Huang’s private life. On Friday he asked whether Nvidia checked its customers. Anyone at the company should be held accountable, he said.

Bessent was speaking on CNBC’s “Squawk Box”. CNBC asked whether Nvidia’s top processors had reached China through Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. Bessent said there was “a lot of leakage in the system”. The government is working to close it down, he added.

“The story has been thus far on Jensen Huang’s personal foibles,” Bessent said. “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?”

“I think it’s important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that,” he said.

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on Thursday. He had admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. US officials suspect she is a Chinese intelligence asset.

Megaspeed secured more than $4bn of Nvidia chips, The New York Times reported. US agents suspected it of smuggling some of them into China. Megaspeed has denied the diversion allegations.

Nvidia banned all sales and shipments to Megaspeed in June 2025, a spokesman told The Wall Street Journal.

Bessent linked the leakage to President Donald Trump’s limit on the Nvidia chips China may receive. Asked if he was frustrated by the delays over Megaspeed, he said:

“I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s.”

“And so any leakage is very frustrating,” he said. It “hurts our great companies in the AI race [and] gives the Chinese an advantage.”

Huang had pushed Washington to ease limits on exporting advanced AI chips to China. In December 2025, Trump said Nvidia could sell its H200 chips to approved Chinese customers. The US would take a percentage of the sales.

Bessent said Treasury, the Pentagon, the State Department and the US Trade Representative had all backed listing Megaspeed. The entity list is the Commerce Department’s trade blacklist. It cuts companies off from US technology. Megaspeed is not on it.

“They were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months, but Commerce has the pen,” Bessent said. “You will have to ask them about their internal processes.”

His remarks came two days after an Axios report. It said Bessent had pressed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over Megaspeed in the White House Situation Room. Commerce spokeswoman Kristen Eichamer said the two had “no such conversation”. Asked about it on Friday, Bessent said:

“We don’t repeat conversations in the Situation Room.”

Commerce did not immediately respond to CNBC about Bessent’s remarks. A Commerce spokesperson told Semafor:

“Treasury and Commerce have a great working relationship.”

Commerce halted its Megaspeed probe in 2025 after Nvidia’s lawyer contacted its agents, the Times reported. The Senate Banking Committee has asked Huang and Lutnick to testify in December.

#3202. Ecopetrol (EC) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Record refining margins met external headwinds this quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Ecopetrol S.A. (EC +0.72%) reported a significant increase in net income for the third quarter of 2026, supported by the integration of its newly acquired Brazilian subsidiary, Brava Energia, and record high refining margins. Management identified five strategic priorities for the company, including reserve additions, strengthening gas supply, and operational efficiency across the business group. The company completed a $2 billion bond issuance to optimize its debt profile and refinance short-term obligations related to its international expansion. Leadership emphasized a strategy focusing on energy security and disciplined capital allocation to restore market confidence and drive sustainable value creation.

Operator: Good morning. My name is Natalia, and I will be your operator today. Welcome to Ecopetrol's earnings conference call, in which we will discuss the main financial and operating results of the third quarter of 2026. There will be a questions and answers session at the end of the presentation. Before we begin, it is important to mention that the comments in this call by Ecopetrol's senior management include projections of the company's future performance. These projections do not constitute any commitment as to future results, nor do they take into account risks or uncertainties that could materialize.

As a result, Ecopetrol assumes no responsibility in the event that future results are different from the projections shared on this conference call. The call will be led by Joaquín Gutiérrez, CEO of Ecopetrol; Camilo Barco, CFO; Elsa Jaimes, Acting Executive Vice President of Hydrocarbons; and Armando Cuello, Executive Vice President of Energies for the Transition. Thank you for your attention. Mr. Gutiérrez, you may begin your conference.

Joaquín Gutiérrez: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Welcome to the first earnings call under the current administration of Ecopetrol and its leadership team. I would like to thank the board of directors for their trust and confidence in appointing me to lead the company. We will work in close coordination with our majority shareholder and government authorities within the framework of our corporate governance standards and the best interests of all shareholders. I'd like to extend a special greeting to our investors, shareholders, and other stakeholders, and reaffirm my commitment to this great project that we have called the new era of Ecopetrol.

This is not a slogan, but rather a strategic direction and a commitment to Colombia, a new era that is already underway to foster the development of the industry, strengthen Ecopetrol's leadership as a driving force of Colombia's energy sector, and unlock strategic projects that are critical to energy security, competitiveness, and growth for both the company and the country. I take on this responsibility, convinced that Ecopetrol possesses high-quality assets, an integrated value chain, recognized technical capabilities, and an exceptional workforce. Through our initial reviews across the organization, we have identified concrete opportunities to reorganize operations more efficiently across the business group, increase reserve additions, develop new gas alternatives, and expand our ability to generate value.

Our path forward can be summarized through five priorities. First, increase reserves by prioritizing profitable barrels, advancing exploration in licensed areas, and evaluating new growth opportunities both inside and outside Colombia. Second, actively participate in the short-term solutions that Colombia requires to strengthen gas and energy supply and contribute to the country's energy security through a new competitive gas offering for regasification alternatives. Third, advance the development of offshore resources to convert their potential into production and value. While fully respecting the fundamental right to prior consultation, we are working with government authorities to better coordinate prior consultation and environmental permitting processes.

Fourth, strengthen legal certainty, restoring market credibility and confidence in Ecopetrol through consistent execution while attracting foreign investment to support our growth projects. Fifth, strengthen our operations through a focus on operational efficiency, prioritizing profitability, cash generation, and competitive returns. We are already reinforcing cost discipline measures. At the parent company level, we will eliminate duplicate activities, reduce rework, and optimize administrative workloads to capture efficiencies. In addition, since my arrival, we have been working alongside the Ministry of Finance on mechanisms to facilitate the monetization of Fuel Price Stabilization Fund and tax receivables through payment offsets.

I would like to highlight the inclusion by the national government of the FEPC-related appropriations in the 2027 national budget, as well as the recent payment corresponding to the third and fourth quarters of the 2025 balance. These actions provide greater visibility regarding funding resources for next year and contribute positively to the group's financial management and liquidity. Likewise, it's important to highlight the removal of the attachment risk associated with the dispute on fuel imports with DIAN, following the authorities' clarification that enforced collections cannot proceed while the matter remains subject to judicial review. The merits of the dispute continue to be addressed through the courts.

Our commitment is to build on the group's strengths and accelerate sustainable value creation. Let's move to the next slide. This agenda requires leadership, governance, and an organization aligned around common objectives. Over the past two months, the general shareholders meeting elected a renewed board of directors, which subsequently established its committees, all chaired by independent members. In addition, new leaders have joined strategic areas of the company and will support the execution of the five priorities I just outlined. We are advancing strategic initiatives for the industry through coordination with government authorities, regional stakeholders, and other interest groups to accelerate projects that are critical to both the company's future and the country's energy security.

Market confidence is not built through announcements. It's built through consistent execution, legal certainty, and measurable results. This is how we intend to lead the rebirth and future of Ecopetrol. Today, we are reporting solid third quarter results that demonstrate the company's ability to capitalize on improved market conditions. Let's move to the next slide. The key message defining this quarter's performance is that our integrated business model once again demonstrated its ability to capture value. As president, I inherit challenges like mature fields and the lower base production in certain assets. However, supported by the strength of our refining, transportation, and commercial businesses, we have delivered strong financial results that provide a solid foundation for achieving our objectives.

During the quarter, we reached a consolidated production of 747,000 bbl of oil equivalent per day, transported 1,000,087 bpd, and recorded refinery throughput of 412,000 bpd. Refining remained the primary value driver during the quarter, supported by a record gross refining margin of $45.6 per bbl, the highest levels ever recorded by the group. Notably, these results were achieved while significant maintenance activities were underway at the Barrancabermeja refinery, demonstrating resilience, reliability, and operational flexibility of our integrated system.

Against this backdrop, and with Brava's initial contribution following its consolidation in September, we delivered COP 4.8 trillion in net income, up 86% year-on-year, an EBITDA margin of 45%, representing an increase of 4 percentage points, and a strong cash position of COP 16.3 trillion. These results benefited from favorable market conditions and progress in our efficiency program, which accumulated COP 4.4 trillion in benefits, approximately 64% of which directly impacted EBITDA, strengthening profitability and financial flexibility across the group. We also reduced deferred production associated with external events by 91% compared to the previous quarter, reflecting a meaningful improvement in the operational security of our assets. In addition, we advanced projects that expand our future growth options.

At Sirius, we made significant progress in mitigating regulatory and socio-environmental risks that had been affecting the project's development schedule. We secured the timely approval of the amendment of the Ballena environmental permit, a key milestone to adapt gas processing infrastructure. We also continue supporting initiatives aimed at streamlining prior consultation processes and improving coordination with environmental permitting requirements, helping ensure the execution of this strategic project for Colombia's energy security. At KGG, we achieved a significant milestone with the approval of the exemption from the environmental alternatives assessment requirement for the project's flow line.

This achievement allows us to continue advancing environmental management activities and supports the development of a strategic initiative to strengthen the gas supply of the country. At Komodo, as a result of the coordinated efforts between Ecopetrol, operating partner Anadarko, and the Colombian government, ANLA enabled the drilling of the exploratory well by removing inappropriate obligations from the environmental license granted in 2024. This milestone makes the execution of a key project for the Ecopetrol Group viable. Finally, the approval of the Orca development plan in Brazil represents an important step toward unlocking an asset with the potential to deliver more than 33,000 net bpd to Ecopetrol.

All of these achievements strengthen our long-term vision and support future reserve additions and production growth. Let's move to the next slide. One of the most important milestones of the quarter was the closing of the acquisition, an issue, the start of the integration process, and the consolidation of Brava. As a result, Brazil becomes a strategic pillar of Ecopetrol's international growth. Providing new opportunities for production, reserves, and exploration. Ecopetrol's consolidated financial results for the quarter include one month of Brava's financial consolidation at 100%, contributing approximately 3% of revenue, 4% of EBITDA, and 2% of net income growth. As such, our investment in Brava generates value from the very beginning of the integration process.

Ecopetrol's third quarter 2026 production, including the full consolidation of Brava, reached 747,000 bbl of oil equivalent per day. Excluding the 49% of non-controlling interest, was approximately 728,000 bbl of oil equivalent per day, keeping us close to our full-year target. The integration phase we are now beginning is just as important as the consolidation phase we have successfully completed. Our focus will be on establishing corporate governance guidelines, integrating financial planning and reporting processes, harmonizing reserves under SEC standards, strengthening controls, and capturing operational and exploration synergies. Most importantly, we want the market to understand that Brava is not just an acquisition.

It is an investment designed to grow profitably and with discipline in Brazil, creating value for all shareholders. The recent approval of the Orca development plan reinforces this vision and strengthens our presence in one of the most important energy provinces in the Americas. Now let us give the floor to Camilo Barco, Vice President of Finance and Sustainable Value, who will provide additional details.

Camilo Barco: Thank you, President, and welcome to the Ecopetrol Group. As we have seen, Ecopetrol's integrated model has once again proven its ability to capture value. Let me walk with you now on how that performance translated into stronger financial results. During the third quarter of 2026, group revenues reached COP 35.1 trillion, up COP 5.2 trillion year-over-year. EBITDA came at COP 15.9 trillion, an increase of COP 3.5 trillion versus the prior year, while net income reached COP 4.8 trillion, up COP 2.2 trillion. Our EBITDA margin stood at 45%, a 4 percentage point improvement versus the same period of 2025. These results already reflect 100% of Brava's contribution for September, as previously discussed.

Its integration marks the beginning of a new phase in which our focus will be on disciplined value capture. The pricing environment was the main driver of these results. Over the first nine months of the year, the average Brent price rose 27%. Our crude basket increased 23%, and our product basket was up 45%. This last increase particularly benefited our refining business, whose share of the group EBITDA rose 15 percentage points year-over-year. Beyond market factors, I would highlight the integrated management of our refineries, crude slate optimization, and commercial coordination, which enabled us to capture favorable differentials and capitalize on this environment.

As a result, the group's integration delivered not only scale, but also agility and greater diversification of results. On a year-to-date basis, net income reached COP 13.7 trillion, up 83%, or roughly COP 6.2 trillion versus the same period of 2025. This includes COP 0.1 trillion contribution to net income following the Brava acquisition. Four factors drove this performance. First, pricing had a positive impact of COP 13.5 trillion. Taken together, higher Brent prices and stronger product differentials offset the weaker negotiated crude differentials. Second, external factors, including a lower exchange rate and inflationary cost pressures, had a negative impact of COP 4.1 trillion.

Third, operational factors reduced net income by COP 1.2 trillion, mainly due to lower sales volumes resulting from lower production. Fourth, a higher tax burden had an impact of COP 2.1 trillion, driven by the wealth tax and the increase in the income tax surcharge, which rose from zero in 2025 to 15% in 2026, in line with the projected Brent price. Year-to-date EBITDA totaled COP 47 trillion. Exploration and production accounted for 50%, refining for 19%, transportation for 16%, and transmission and toll roads for 15%. This mix highlights the complementary nature of our businesses and their ability to offset pressures across segments.

Turning to working capital, the FEPC received stood at COP 11.4 trillion at the end of September. This balance includes COP 1.6 trillion still standing from 2025, as well as amounts accrued between January and September 2026. Acceleration collections and identifying alternatives to limit further accumulation remains priorities to protect our liquidity. On leverage, our gross debt-to-EBITDA ratio stood at 2.1x at the group level and 1.5x excluding ISA. These levels reflect the consolidation and financing of Brava and remain within our ceiling of 2.5x. Let's move to the next slide. We closed September with a solid liquidity position and a cash balance of COP 16.3 trillion, including COP 3.1 trillion from Brava.

This position was mainly supported by operating cash generation and the collection of FEPC receivables for the third and fourth quarters of 2025. Operating cash flow reached COP 22 trillion, funding our investment plan, debt service, and dividend payments while preserving our financial flexibility. Year-to-date organic investment totaled $4.8 billion. We allocated 65% to hydrocarbons, 27% to transmission and toll roads, and 8% to energy transition businesses. Our priority was clear: ensure operational continuity, strengthen our core businesses, and advance selectively on growth projects. Of the total, 65% was deployed in Colombia and 35% in our international operations.

Within hydrocarbons, investments was mainly focused on exploration and production, particularly in assets in Meta and the Permian Basin, as well as projects in Brazil. We also invested in gas refining and the continuity of our transportation systems. In addition, inorganic investments totaled $1.4 billion, including the acquisition of Brava in Brazil, the stake in Madeira assets at ISA Brasil, and the entry contribution to the Génova project. Efficiency also contributed to value creation, totaling COP 4.4 trillion through September. Of this amount, COP 2.8 trillion benefited EBITDA, mainly in hydrocarbons, COP 0.9 trillion came from CapEx optimization, and COP 0.7 trillion from working capital. This program strengthens our margins and frees up resources for operations and growth.

On the debt side, we continue to proactively manage our liability profile to extend maturities, reduce refinancing risk, and preserve the company's liquidity and financial flexibility. In line with this approach, we completed a $2 billion international bond offering 2034. The proceeds will be used to fully refinance the short-term loan used to acquire a stake in Brava and to prepay $810 million of our 2029 bonds. This transaction replaces existing debt and does not increase our overall indebtedness. The order book reached 3.5 times the amount placed, the highest level in the last five years.

The strength and diversification of demand allowed us to achieve the tightest spread to both the sovereign and US Treasuries for an Ecopetrol international issuance for that period, with a new issue concession close to zero. These terms reflect investor confidence and our ability to access international capital markets on competitive terms. Now let's move to the next slide to show how this transaction improves our maturity profile. First, we are eliminating from the group the 2027 maturity of approximately $1.2 billion on the bridge loan taken out to acquire Brava, which brings that year's commitments down to $609 million.

Second, we expect to reduce the 2029 maturities to $1.1 billion, and we are replacing debt carrying an 8.625% coupon with a debt carrying a 7.875% coupon. Third, we are shifting these commitments to 2034, a year with no maturities, which extends the average life of our debt and better distributes our obligations over time. As a result, between 2027 and 2029, our annual maturities remain below $1.1 billion. This gives us a more balanced debt profile, lower short and medium-term refinancing needs, and the financial capacity to address the company's priorities. It is important to note that the 2029 bonds will be redeemed on November 19, 2026.

With that, I will hand it over to Elsa Jaimes, our Acting Executive Vice President of Hydrocarbons, who will walk you through our operating results.

Elsa Jaimes: Thank you, Camilo. in exploration, we continued to strengthen our resource addition and long-term growth strategy. As of September, we had drilled nine wells, achieving our annual program ahead of schedule and delivering three discoveries while advancing additional exploration activities planned for the fourth quarter. With the completion of the drilling activities at the Sandía well and Petrobras, we concluded the largest deepwater exploration campaign ever undertaken in the Colombian Caribbean. Over more than two years of continuous operations, five exploration wells were drilled, representing close to $1 billion in investment while maintaining the highest operational safety standards.

Regarding the Sirius project, we continue to advance engineering, environmental, and social studies, as well as the prior consultation process with communities within the area of influence. We remain on track to submit the environmental impact assessment for both the field development and the subsea flow line during the first quarter of 2027. Meanwhile, Orca Brazil reached a significant milestone on August 7 with the approval of its development plan of the ANP. This achievement, together with the progress made in the construction of the floating production storage and offloading vessel, or FPSO, continues to support the development of an asset expected to contribute more than 33,000 bpd of net production of Ecopetrol beginning 2029.

On the production front, we highlight the contribution of our new subsidiary, Brava Energia, which added 39,000 bpd, supporting total group production of 747,000 bpd. In Colombia, 91% reduction in deferred volumes associated with external events compared to the previous quarter supported the gradual recovery of crude oil production, partially upsetting natural field decline and other operational constraints. In Permian, performance remains aligned with its development plan, and production is expected to close within the range of 83,000 bbl of oil equivalent per day.

During the fourth quarter, we continue executing our production assurance plan, supported by new water handling capacity, the development of new wells in strategic assets across Colombia and the Permian Basin, and the advancement of water injection recovery initiatives of CPO-09. These efforts strengthen base production sustainability through targeted well intervention programs. As a result, the segment delivered solid operational and financial performance, reaching a year-to-date EBITDA margin of 41% as of September. Additionally, the incorporation of Brava's production volumes enhances the resilience of our production platform and supports the delivery of our production guidance while mitigating the impact of external events and operational restrictions experienced throughout the year.

At the same time, it expands our long-term growth runway and strengthens our capacity to create sustainable value for shareholders. In the refining segment, we delivered another exceptional quarter, reaching new all-time highs in integrated gross refining margin, EBITDA, and EBITDA margin. Favorable fuel market dynamics and our strong value capture capabilities enabled us to achieve a record gross refining margin of $45.6 per bbl, up 53% versus the previous quarter, and more than three times the level recorded a year ago. These results were achieved despite major maintenance activities carried out at the Barrancabermeja refinery, which temporarily reduced integrated throughput to 412,000 bpd.

As a result, the segment delivered a record EBITDA of COP 4.1 trillion and a historic EBITDA margin of 19%, highlighting the strength and resilience of our integrated hydrocarbons value chain. Turning to the transportation segment, we transported more than 1.1 million bpd during the quarter, maintaining system reliability and flexibility despite the major maintenance activities in refining. This performance was supported by incremental volumes, the transportation of imported crude, and the optimization of logistics corridors and inventory management. Although EBITDA decreased compared to the same period last year, primarily due to foreign exchange effects, the segment maintained solid operating performance and continued to support the flexibility and reliability of our integrated system. Let's move on to profitability and cost.

During the first nine months of 2026, the hydrocarbon segment further strengthened its profitability, primarily supported by a more favorable commodity price environment. EBITDA reached COP 39.3 trillion, a 32% increase compared to the same period of 2025, while the EBITDA margin expanded from 38%-45%. On the cost front, we continued to execute productivity, operational efficiency, and resource optimization initiatives that helped partially offset external cost pressures, particularly those associated with the appreciation of the Colombian peso, inflationary effects, and higher electricity tariffs driven by El Niño weather phenomenon. Lifting costs decreased 3.3% in local currency terms compared with the same period of the year before, reaching COP 47,192 per bbl.

Excluding foreign exchange effects, lifting costs stood at $11.4 per bbl, below the $11.8 per bbl reported a year ago, and our $12 per bbl reference target for 2026. This performance was supported by higher monetization volumes, as well as efficiencies captured across maintenance activities, operating services, digital infrastructure, and energy consumption. Similarly, refining cash costs declined by 2% in local currency terms, improving from COP 23,219 pesos to COP 22,750 per barrel. Excluding foreign exchange effects, refining cash costs stood at $5.5 per bbl compared to $5.6 per bbl n the same period of the prior year, supported by higher refinery throughput and disciplined cost management.

Cost per barrel transported increased by 9.3%, mainly reflecting higher operational requirements associated with emergency response efforts and challenging operating conditions. Overall, these results demonstrate our ability to translate a favorable market environment into stronger profitability while maintaining strict cost discipline to offset external pressures. I will now turn the call over to Armando, who will provide an update on the energies for the transition business line.

Armando Cuello: Thank you, Elsa. During 2026, we saw a significant shift in global LNG market dynamics at the beginning of the year. The market was characterized by growing supply and relatively balanced conditions, with international benchmarks like TTF and JKM at around $10-$11 per million BTUs. However, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East rapidly changed this environment, affecting flows equivalent to about 18% of global LNG supply and resulting in a market increasingly constrained by the availability of LNG molecules. This environment intensified competition between Europe and Asia for available cargoes and pushed TTF prices to $33 per million BTUs by the end of 2026.

This represented an increase of about 200%, reaching the highest level seen in the last four years and reflecting growing market concerns over security of supply. Against this backdrop, suppliers prioritized TTF index structures or sought to capture the price expectations embedded in that market, significantly reducing the availability of competitive offers for buyers such as Ecopetrol. As a result, the economic conditions observed during the period did not allow us to move forward with LNG purchases that met Ecopetrol's criteria for competitiveness, profitability, and appropriate risk management. For this reason, we maintained a disciplined approach and decided not to proceed with LNG procurement processes for the Puerto Bahía and Buenaventura terminals under current market conditions.

Nevertheless, at Ecopetrol, we continue making our best efforts to identify competitive supply opportunities while maintaining the commitments established under our sales contracts with domestic market participants and seeking to align supply availability with the scheduled startup dates of the regasification facilities. Consistent with this strategy, regasification projects continue to progress in line with their expected startup schedules. The Pacific regasification facility is approximately 90% complete and remains on track to begin operations by year-end 2026, while the Caribbean regasification facility has reached 53% completion and is expected to begin operations during the first quarter of 2027.

These initiatives, together with the development of offshore and onshore resources, will expand supply options and contribute to strengthening energy security and the reliability of Colombia's gas market. Next slide. Regarding domestic supply during the third quarter of 2026, Ecopetrol maintained its position as the only domestic producer to offer and allocate firm gas volumes to the market. During the quarter, we allocated additional volumes from Cupiagua, complemented by new production sources in Huila. These actions allowed us to make additional gas volumes available to the market, contributing to the reliability of domestic supply. Ecopetrol also actively contributed and responded promptly to operational events affecting the system.

During the scheduled maintenance of the SPEC regasification terminal between July 30 and August 3, we marketed 97 GBTUD to help meet thermal generation and essential demand. Subsequently, during the operational contingency at SPEC in September, we increased the availability of gas from Cusiana and Cupiagua by 5 GBTUD for six days, helping mitigate the impact on regulated demand and the national transportation system. More recently, on October 27, we increased supply by an additional 5 GBTUD to support the system during the contingency resulting from the scheduled curtailment associated with another SPEC shutdown. This contributed to maintaining the operational stability of the pipeline system until SPEC resumed normal operations. Next.

Regarding energy management, we continued implementing initiatives aimed at strengthening the group's competitiveness and reducing our exposure to price volatility associated with El Niño and the spot electricity market. First, through our energy efficiency program, we achieved cumulative optimization of 2.66 PJs, equivalent to almost twice the annual energy consumption of the Rubiales field, generating savings of approximately COP 68 billion. This allowed us to reduce the group's energy requirements and consequently our exposure to increased energy supply costs. In addition, the group's renewable energy portfolio reached 1,210 MW, including assets in operation and under construction and development, as well as market-based power supply contracts.

Our operating assets continue to generate efficiencies, delivering savings of COP 6.1 billion during the period, driven by the lower cost of energy consumed compared with market purchasing alternatives. During the quarter, we continued to make progress on the Windpeshi wind project, which reached 25% overall completion, development of the interconnection line, and securing the land required for project execution. In addition, together with our partner, AES, we continue structuring the JK1 and JK2 wind projects. Our financial advisors, IDB and Bancolombia, are currently conducting due diligence, and we expect to reach financial close and FID during the first quarter of 2027.

These initiatives, together with our self-generation capacity and contracting in the wholesale electricity market, allowed us to cover 92.6% of the group's energy demand, reducing our exposure to the spot market and strengthening operational resilience under climate-related stress scenarios. Through a combination of conventional self-generation on-site and remote renewable self-generation and active contracting management, our purchases in the wholesale electricity market were made at average prices of 8.5% below regulated market benchmarks, contributing to greater stability in the group's energy costs. Overall, these results reflect Ecopetrol's commitment to energy security, the timely development of strategic infrastructure, the incorporation of new energy sources, and the delivery of operational efficiencies that strengthen the sustainability and competitiveness of our business.

Thank you so much. Now, we'll hand it over to our CEO.

Joaquín Gutiérrez: Let me conclude this presentation with a reflection on the environment that we're facing and our priorities going forward. We are operating in a context marked by geopolitical volatility, higher logistics costs, pressure on capital, and challenges in sustaining organic production. In addition, we have seen wider discounts on certain crudes relative to Brent and greater volatility in refined product differentials, reflecting an energy market that remains tight and subject to supply and global logistics disruptions. In this context, our organic production is declining as fields mature, and it requires exploration and sustained investment to boost volumes. Yet, amid these challenges, Ecopetrol has distinctive strengths to navigate this environment.

We have an increasingly flexible commercial platform and a portfolio of opportunities that includes Brava, Sirius, Orca, and our recent exploration successes. In gas, in particular, we are simultaneously advancing on short, medium, and long-term solutions that contribute to the country's energy security and allow us to monetize the potential of our resources. We have the ability to capture value through an integrated model that combines production, transportation, refining, marketing, and a growing international presence, as reflected in the results we have presented. This new stage demands that we go further, and our priority is to transform Ecopetrol so we can do things differently and prepare it for new opportunities and challenges.

That is why our focus is on organizational and operational transformation to raise productivity, efficiency, and profitability across the Ecopetrol Group by simplifying processes, eliminating rework, and reducing costs through rigorous capital allocation. We will achieve excellence in the execution and delivery of strategic projects by accelerating strategic decision-making, and we will build a more efficient organization based on delivering results. The progress presented today shows that this transformation is already underway. We are unlocking strategic projects, strengthening institutional coordination, mitigating material risks for the company, and advancing initiatives that have a tangible impact on our growth prospects, competitiveness, and value creation.

Opportunities are important, but what truly matters is our ability to turn them into concrete, tangible, and demonstrable results. That will be the measure of this new era of rebirth, a more agile and competitive Ecopetrol, capable of turning opportunities into sustainable results, where we can strengthen reserves, develop gas, improve profitability, preserve a solid financial position, and create sustainable value for our shareholders. All of this alongside our employees, whom I thank for their commitment and dedication, as well as our investors, clients, communities, and other stakeholders for their trust. May determination guide our decisions, and may the future of Colombia be the goal we never stop pursuing.

Welcome once again to the new era of the crown jewel of the nation, the company we will defend because it belongs to all Colombians by nature. Welcome to the rebirth that will mark the beginning of a new chapter for Ecopetrol and for all of Colombia. Thank you very much. With this, we begin the Q&A session.

Joaquín Gutiérrez: Thank you. Andrés? Thank you so much for your good wishes. Let me respond to your questions. The international promotion is a leverage to expand reserves and production. Every investment made overseas has to compete with the same rigor for capital than any project within Colombia. In terms of Venezuela, in my recent visit there, I confirmed that there are real opportunities there, both in gas and as in oil and gas. The closest is the gas line, Antonio Ricaurte.

The national government of Colombia said it was a strategic project. ANLA confirmed the firmness of its license, and we as Ecopetrol will request to PDVSA to grant us the operation of the Colombian section, the 88 km in Colombia. We are renegotiating a contract of sale at a price that is very competitive. It will be below what we have today in the market. As to oil, we see opportunities to add consolidated reserves, but I would like to be clear. We are a company. We requested the license for the gas line because we are a company that meets, and we will not take a step beyond that framework.

Venezuela is a great opportunity, yes, but it will not be a dependence. It gives production cash and especially experience of non-conventionals, especially to bring that to Colombia. Would we be interested in growing? We will grow, or better, we will grow where value is. In short, Andrés, Colombia first and the world where there is value second. I ask you to please measure us quarter by quarter, always based on results.

The Sirius project, Petrobras, as an operator, made the request in 2025, and that session or those discussions with the government were retaken with the new government along with the institutions, and we are advancing with this. Petrobras has held several sessions, work sessions with the Ministry, contributing information that has been requested. I just wanted to complement this.

Andres Duarte: Thank you so much. What I affirm in terms as being an operator, am I wrong or not? Thank you.

Joaquín Gutiérrez: I referred at the Antonio Ricaurte operator. I did not answer that part of the question. I am sorry. Yes, indeed, we are in the process of negotiation directly with PDVSA so we can make the operation, but only of the 88 km that are within Colombia. We can guarantee that way that the supply will not have any problem or affectation. We prefer to make that specific operation, and that is what we are requesting to PDVSA, and we will make a contract for that specific operation headed by Sirius, one of our subsidiaries. For that, I already told you that we requested the OFAC license because we need that license.

If granted, we can advance in that negotiation and we can have the operation. But again, it is only the 88 km on the side of Colombia.

Operator: The next question is from Steffania Mosquera from Credicorp Capital. Ms. Mosquera, the floor is yours.

Steffania Mosquera: Okay, thank you. My question is especially about a disinvestment that eventually could be made by the government, a partial disinvestment of the government of Ecopetrol. What is your vision about that? We have lately heard news about the Centro Democrático saying that 8% of Ecopetrol should be sold, and the last tax reform mentions the possibility that the President has special powers to cut down Act 226. What do you think, considering that eventual disinvestment would be an increase of the floating, which would be key for the inclusion of Ecopetrol in international index, and in turn could result in significant increases of liquidity and price?

Camilo Barco: Steffania, good morning, and thank you for your questions. This is Camilo Barco. Basically, I would think that this question is more for our majority shareholders to answer. It is a decision that should be made by the national government to evaluate what to do with its property over Ecopetrol. We really have no comments on this. Nothing different to what you have mentioned. It would have surely a positive effect on the capital's market related to the floating of the company. But again, when it comes to the decision made by the government and its share or its stake in Ecopetrol, we cannot answer here what the government will do.

Operator: Let us continue with Ricardo Sandoval from Cibest. Mr. Sandoval, the floor is yours.

Ricardo Sandoval: Hello, everyone. Thank you for the call, and the best wishes for Joaquín. I have a question. The conversion of the oil pipe that was set to be made to give feasibility to the new regasification of the Caribbean. I mean, is that conversion something that will take away capability to take out future volumes in the Magdalena Medio and in the western mountain range? Is that conversion still underway as we have been talking about the Puerto Bahía? Is there a way to get out of this? It goes really against what the government wants to promote fracking at the most. That is my question. Thank you.

Nubia Stella: Good morning. This is Nubia Stella. I am the Acting President of Cenit Ricardo, thank you for your question. We, as leaders of the mixing group, are exploring different alternatives to enable the logistics necessary to develop the fields. Today, we have not ruled out any option. We are exploring and reviewing all the options that we have. As of today, we are still working on this without any specific decision on a particular project. Thank you.

Armando Cuello: I am Armando Cuello, VP for Energies of Transition. Regarding the Puerto Bahía regasification system, we are doing well. We are advancing. We think that the first two months of next year will be commissioned, and we think it is fundamental for the country's energy security. We will not have the LNG. We will not be depending only on the SPEC regasification. We are not going to be pulling out. We think it is very important for the country and for Ecopetrol. Thank you.

Mauricio Gutiérrez: Ricardo, good morning. This is Mauricio Gutiérrez, VP of Strategy and New Businesses. Regarding your consideration on Puerto Bahía and the non-conventional fields, our observations are focused on the idea that both projects contribute to the energy safety of the country, and not necessarily advance against each other or not regarding each other. With this, the opportunities of non-conventional fields in Magdalena Medio open great opportunities, which reflect the commitment of this administration to non-conventional fields with two new reserve sources, and the regasification system of Puerto Bahía will guarantee the supply of gas that we have needed, where we will be needing in that short and medium term prior to the commissioning of Sirius, which is strategic to us.

We cannot consider that they go against each other, and both projects are complementary. They do not substitute each other, and allows us to guarantee the energy safety in the country. Thank you for your question.

Operator: Last question comes from Alejandra Andrade from JPMorgan. Alejandra,

Alejandra Andrade: thank you for taking my question. Specifically, I would like to ask, you already made an issuance of bonds and to refinance the Brava loan and to pay bonds that matured in 2029, but are you considering to do something more in 2027 in the international capital market, or are you waiting for an option of that sort?

Camilo Barco: Alejandra, good morning, and thank you for your question. Let me take this opportunity to thank especially the analysts and the representatives of the bondholders and the investors' communities that have shown us in this issuance their trust and optimism over Ecopetrol. I said we are very happy.It was an issue that was interesting, not only with the amount offered, but with the demand that was so significant that exceeded 3.5 times the capital offered and led to conditions that you know well, that are very favorable for Ecopetrol with historical records over the US Treasuries and within the curve of the sovereign bonds with a minimum difference of 80 basis points over the debt of Colombia.

We are happy, satisfied. It was a significant transaction. With this, we believe that in 2026, we have defined the capital structure. Towards the future, it is important to mention what we have said before. We are monitoring constantly the market. In 2027, we will continue working on every front in banking financing and opportunities that may rise through the capital market.

I hope with this, I have answered your question. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. Now we close the Q&A session, and we give way to Joaquín Gutiérrez, the CEO of Ecopetrol, for final remarks.

Joaquín Gutiérrez: Before I say goodbye, I would like to thank you for your time, for your questions, and above all, for your trust. Today, we have shown you the numbers, but I want to give you more. The certainty that we know where we are headed. We know our challenges, and we will not hide. We have the technical talent, the assets, and a clear plan to move from a horizon of reserves to one of decades, with discipline in each prize and a corporate governance that is among those of the best oil companies of the world. Again, I do not ask you to believe my words.

I ask you to look at us based on our results quarter by quarter, because that is the only language we will be talking. Ecopetrol will make it, and those that are with us today will be part of that story. Thank you. Because when Ecopetrol lifts, Colombia lifts. Welcome to the rebirth of Ecopetrol. Have a good day.

#3201. Disney is now embracing the AI it once fought, from cartoons to finance

An AI-animated kids' show is coming to Disney+ as CEO Josh D'Amaro brings AI into every part of the company.

The Alameda Avenue entrance to the Walt Disney Studios in Burbank, California, in July 2016.

Disney will bring Ozzy Fox, a kids’ series animated with AI tools, to Disney+ in December, Bloomberg reported. Under CEO Josh D’Amaro, it is also using AI in finance, streaming suggestions and its parks, while still guarding its characters.

Disney, which once sued AI companies over its characters, is now putting the technology to work across the company, Bloomberg reported. In December, it will bring Ozzy Fox, a children’s series animated with AI, to Disney+.

Ozzy Fox was made with French startup Animaj, whose tools turn artists’ drawings and text instructions into 3D animation. It first appeared on YouTube in July, where some viewers called it “AI slop”.

The push is led by CEO Josh D’Amaro, who took over this year. A week into his tenure, OpenAI shut down its Sora video app, ending a planned deal for Disney to license its characters to it.

“We’re being very aggressive about exploring emerging technologies,” D’Amaro said at a company event this month.

In September, Disney named Character.AI’s chief executive, Karandeep Anand, as its first CTO. It has since bid $20M for some of the assets of the bankrupt chatbot startup, which could one day let Disney+ users talk to characters.

Disney still guards its characters closely. Rather than license them to AI firms, it has signed a deal letting Adobe build AI models on them under its control.

Apple TV has announced a new comedy, She’s Fine, that’s coming soon with stars Elizabeth Banks and Ted Danson. Here are the details.

Earlier this year, Apple announced a high-profile new comedy in the works starring Elizabeth Banks, with later cast additions including Ted Danson and guest star Tom Selleck.

Now today that series, titled ‘She’s Fine,’ has gotten a release date and the first images have debuted.

She’s Fine premieres Wednesday, January 27 with two episodes, followed by weekly releases through March 24.

Fresh off a messy divorce, Heidi (Banks) sets out to secure a lively second act for herself and her kids. But when she stumbles into coordinating her father’s retirement community sexcapades, Heidi is forced into an unlikely alliance with his girlfriend’s perpetually single son.

Katey Sagal and Rob Delaney also star in the half-hour comedy, which hails from creators Liz Heldens and Matt Ward.

Other notable Apple TV comedies include the Owen Wilson-starring Stick, which just returned for season 2. And Bad Monkey from the co-creator of Ted Lasso and Shrinking is coming back soon too.

Are you interested in watching She’s Fine? Let us know in the comments.

#3197. GridAI to buy Wyoming gas firm Pronghorn to power AI data centres

The small Nasdaq company wants to turn gas fields into power for AI, starting with 300 MW in 2027.

GridAI Technologies has agreed to buy Wyoming natural gas producer Pronghorn Resources in an all-stock deal. It plans to build gas-fired power plants for AI data centres, aiming for 300 MW in 2027, but has no named customers yet.

GridAI Technologies has agreed to buy Pronghorn Resources, a natural gas producer in Wyoming, to power AI data centres, the company announced on Thursday. It aims to deliver its first 300 MW of power in 2027.

Pronghorn produces nearly 100 million cubic feet of gas a day from about 3,200 wells in the Powder River Basin. It also owns more than 450 miles of pipelines and has rights to nearly 1 million acres of land and minerals.

GridAI plans to build gas-fired power plants that feed data centres directly, so customers do not have to wait years for a grid connection. It says Pronghorn’s current gas could fuel about 600 MW of power, but that is an estimate. The plants still need to be built and paid for.

The deal is paid in shares, not cash. Pronghorn’s owners will get about 1.25 million GridAI shares plus preferred stock, and the deal is expected to close by 22 November. GridAI, which trades on Nasdaq, was worth about $31M in October, according to StockAnalysis.

GridAI is also taking Wyoming rights to a planned small nuclear reactor design, though it says gas remains its focus for now. It has not named any customers. Last week, Crusoe gave up its Wyoming site to Google, reportedly after failing to find enough customers.

Wyoming is drawing AI investment as other places push back. Google plans a $17B data centre there that will run mainly on gas. Meanwhile, US voters rejected data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures this month, as AI fuels a gas-plant boom.

#3196. Energous (WATT) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Pilots are giving way to rollouts as a major program eyes its first full conversion in 2027.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Energous Corporation (WATT -11.27%) reported consecutive quarterly revenue growth and gross margin improvement as the company moved from technology validation to commercial deployment. Management stated that the company is developing a physical data layer for enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) by combining wireless power with battery-free sensing. The company reported an expansion in its proof-of-concept pipeline through the AWS channel and expects to convert a major program to full deployment in the first quarter of 2027.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Energous Wireless Power Solutions Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please note, this event is being recorded. As a reminder, during today's call, the company will make forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to inherent risks and uncertainties detailed in the company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Actual results may differ materially from those anticipated. Except as otherwise required by federal law, Energous disclaims any obligation to publicly release updates or revisions to any forward-looking statements to reflect changes in expectations. I would now like to turn the conference call over to Mallorie Burak Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of Energous.

Mallorie Burak: Thank you, and welcome, everyone, to the Energous Wireless Power Solutions Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. For those newer to the Energous story, I would encourage you to review the replay of our first quarter call, which provides a full company overview and our second quarter call, which lays out the commercial framework I will build upon today. I will keep the background brief and focus on what has changed and what is building. At its core, Energous is an end-to-end Ambient IoT platform delivering battery-free sensing and real-time operational intelligence. We are building the physical data layer foundation for enterprise AI.

By combining wireless power, battery-free sensing and intelligent data infrastructure, our products enable continuous real-time visibility into assets, inventory and operations, helping enterprises move from simply tracking what's happening to predicting what might happen next and taking action. This intelligence enables companies to mitigate annualized losses stemming from spoilage, inventory shrinkage as well as operating costs resulting from manual tracking methods like RFID. Since pivoting our strategic vision away from consumer IoT to enterprise wireless power solutions in 2022, our focus has been to move from technology validation to commercial adoption at the largest enterprises in the world.

While our sequential quarterly revenue growth underscores the commercial adoption of our product offerings is underway, we believe that the fourth quarter will more clearly demonstrate that the rate of adoption is ramping as our largest customers are expanding in scope and use cases, our shipments continue to build, and our pipeline is beginning to produce specific conversion milestones. In terms of today's agenda, I will start with our operating highlights and the financial headlines, including our gross margin recovery path. Giampaolo will then give a detailed update on each of our customer programs and the sales pipeline, including how programs convert from proof of concept to deployment.

Greg will walk through the financials in detail, and I will return briefly with a few concluding thoughts. Since our Power Bridge transmitter began shipping in 2024, through September 30, 2026, we have shipped over 6,500 transmitters, primarily driven by demand for our 2-watt Power Bridge Pro. The sequential increases in quarterly shipments that began in the fourth quarter of 2025, reflects the shift from technology validation to commercial adoption of our wireless power networks. The third quarter continued the trend of consecutive quarterly revenue growth. We recorded $3.4 million of revenue in the third quarter up approximately 10% from the $3.1 million reported in the second quarter.

We expect sequential growth to continue and to accelerate in the fourth quarter. Gross margin for the third quarter was approximately 14%, a meaningful improvement from the second quarter as the factors we described last quarter began to ease and our July price increase took effect. On our last conference call, we described the retooling, component costs and customer prioritization factors that reduced second quarter margins and we said that we expected margins to progressively recover. Greg will cover the third quarter drivers of this, including the effect of the July price increase. Also on our second quarter conference call, we shared that we were working towards limited production volume at our overseas contract manufacturer during the quarter.

In the third quarter, however, all units sourced came from our U.S. contract manufacturer. The reason stems back to what we described last quarter. The production line upgrades needed to -- needed at our overseas contract manufacturer to support the enhanced product design were still being completed during the third quarter so volume there has not yet begun. Despite that, we still recognized improvement in our gross margin primarily attributable to the price increases implemented in July. Looking to the fourth quarter, both our U.S. and overseas contract manufacturers are producing at volumes.

As a result, we expect fourth quarter gross margins to improve quarter-over-quarter, and we estimate returning to our historical hardware margin levels in the mid-30% range during the first half of 2027. Our long-term objective remains achieving gross margins of 40% or better. I will now turn it over to Giampaolo, our Chief Strategy and Growth Officer, to discuss our customer programs, our pipeline and the commercial dynamics we are seeing. Giampaolo?

Giampaolo Marino: Thank you, Mallorie. I intend to cover for areas today and update on fewer of our active commercial deployment, where our proof-of-concept program stand and where we expect them to convert. What we are hearing from enterprise customers about data and how our software platform feeds into the equation. Our enterprise adoption is advancing across manufacturing, retail and cold chain. The most important shift this year is that the focus is moving from pilots to broader deployments. While at the same time, our customers are expanding the use cases they run on our network, including sale of inventory condition monitoring and asset tracking.

Active commercial deployments, starting with our largest retail customer portion and companies, we are now working with them on additional use cases, which they intend to begin rolling out across their superstore format in 2027. This customer has over 500 superstores in the United States and the scale per location matter. A supercenter requires over 125 bridges compared with roughly 10 to 15 bridges for a standard store. The same customers warehouse cloud division is planned to deploy across approximately 150 locations at about 15 bridges per location. We expect that rollout to begin in early 2027 and continue throughout the year.

Looking out over the next 12 months, we expect demand from these Fortune 10 customers to continue 2 levels. This customer is also evaluating a potential expansion into Canada across their regular retail format, which will require new regulatory approvals for the Power Bridge Pro in that jurisdiction. Infrastructure requirements in that region are still being determined. Fleet and distribution center application continue to be explored, both involve more complex infrastructure, which our customer is assessing. Turning to our Fortune 10 e-commerce customer. Based on that customer's current planning, we continue to expect growth over the next 12 months. Deployment had and will continue across Europe.

We expect to see acceleration in deployment in the U.S. where we are still in the very early stage of opportunity completion with this customer. Use case continued to expand as well and we are now looking at an expansion opportunities in virtual. While we are limited in what we can share in greater detail, in 2027, we expect revenue from this customer to exceed 2026. We share both of these updates today to provide confidence to our investors that we believe our revenue base looking forward is stronger and set up for continued growth. Our largest customers are strong supporters of our technology and are still in the early stages of their adoption cycle.

Because it is the question we frequently received, I would like to spend some time discussing our sales conversion and where active programs currently stand. Our framework has not changed. A program begins with an alignment phase to agree on goals and metrics, typically lasting about a month. A proof of concept follows generally lasting up to 3 months. Successful programs might then expand to multiple trials or move to commercial deployment. With the current sales cycle spanning approximately 6 to 9 months versus 18 to 24 months historically, programs now move faster, but we judge progress by stage advancement not by the number of trials. We also recognize that we have not announced named customers at this year.

Many of our customers do not permit disclosure, and we will not name a customer without permission. What we can do is tell you where some of the more advanced programs are by stage. Several end-to-end proof-of-concept trials are currently active. The first is with a large semi-perishable consumer product manufacturer. It is nearly completion, and we currently expect the customers to move to deployment in the first quarter of 2027. If that happens as planned, it will be the first of our end-to-end solution programs to convert from our proof-of-concept pipeline to a deployment, creating a recurring revenue stream generated from our end-to-end solution, anchored by the monitoring and analytics provided by our SaaS platform e-Compass.

The second proof of concept, which we introduced last quarter is with our regional supercenter and grocery chain operating hundreds of stores across the Midwestern United States. Building on that data generated in the initial phase, we are now working with the customers to define Phase II around measurable business outcomes, reducing shrink, lowering scanning, hardware and maintenance costs and improving labor efficiency and supporting e-commerce growth. The planned scope includes tracking goods between distribution centers and stores, improving shipment manifest accuracy and integrating physical world data into existing enterprise system and analytics. The focus is on validating how our end-to-end solution can deliver operational and financial value, while fitting into the customers' day-to-day workflows.

Beyond those 2 opportunities, we are exploring additional end-to-end proof-of-concept initiatives: one, notably in the health care space, where the Fortune 10 health care retailer had previously completed a proof of concept through a channel partner has chosen to reengage directly to test our full scope solution. Our strategic partnership with AWS continues to strengthen, serving as an important channel for expanding Energous' enterprise reach and accelerating adoption of our end-to-end ambient IoT platform. Customer engagement through the AWS channel has reached a new high with a growing number of active proof-of-concept programs and joint opportunities.

This momentum is also reflected in the AWS recently increasing its reporting highlight customer launches from more than 50% to more than 100, an encouraging indicator of broader customer adoption across the AWS partner ecosystem. Energous continues to expand its presence in the AWS marketplace with 3 qualified device alongside our e-Compass software platform and our e-Sense battery-free sensing technology. Together, this offering provides enterprise customers with access to our integrated wireless power, sensing and data infrastructure solution. Looking ahead, we expect our collaboration with AWS to remain an important driver of pipeline development, customer acquisition and future development opportunity as joint co-selling initiative progress and existing program advanced towards the broader commercialization.

Our national quick service restaurant program remains active. As we discussed last quarter, this customer completed its initial proof of concept in food preparation and cold storage environment. They continue to evaluate different solutions, although we are only supplying the PowerBridge transmitters for this particular proof of concept, we believe the value proposition of using battery-free wireless technology remains a compelling solution for this use case. Our data strategy. As enterprise expand AI into physical operations, they will need reliable, timely data about what is happening across their assets, inventory and facilities. Energous strategy is to address that need through an integrated solution spending persistent energy, connected sensing and trusted physical data infrastructure.

Our focus is on delivering actionable data into customers' existing systems with customer retaining control of their data and how it is used. Central to this strategy is the evolution of the e-Compass into our Layer 3 platform. The software layer that turns physical world sensor readings into contextualized usable data and events for enterprise applications. Our road map includes enterprise APIs real-time event processing, AI assisted infrastructure management and trusted physical data service. Together, these capabilities are intended to help customers assess data quality, monitor infrastructure performance and integrate physical intelligence into their operational scale.

We are pursuing strategic integration and partnership with enterprise IoT, supply chain and AI software providers to extend the value of our platform beyond hardware deployment. By delivering persistent trusted and contextualized physical world data directly into enterprise intelligence and decision-making systems, Energous aims to enable continuous operational visibility, predictive insight and increasingly automated workflow at scale. We believe that this strategy will create opportunities for recurring revenue through infrastructure management and physical data service, while allowing our partner to deliver specialized analytics, applications and business outcomes.

Although this initiative remains at an early stage, with no assurance of recurring resulting agreement or revenue, our strategic direction is clear: To establish Energous as the foundational physical data infrastructure platform for enterprise AI and physical AI. I will now turn it over to Greg.

Gregory Sadikoff: Thank you, Giampaolo. Good afternoon. I will now review Energous' financial results for the third quarter and 9 months ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter financial results. As of September 30, 2026, the company's cash and cash equivalents were $28.8 million. No shares were sold under the ATM program during the third quarter. I will now turn the call back to Mallorie.

The market is beginning to recognize that physical AI requires the ability to continuously generate trusted data from the physical world, and we believe that capability begins with persistent energy. We believe it begins with Energous technology.

As physical AI evolves, one reality is becoming clear. Intelligence is only as reliable as the physical data that powers it. Continuous data requires persistent sensing and persistent sensing requires persistent energy. This is where we believe Energous becomes foundational to the physical AI ecosystem. There’s no shortage of note-taking apps on the App Store, but Apple Notes has long been my favorite, and in iOS 27.3 it’s gaining a new advantage: extensive app controls via Siri AI.

Voice-driven computing is on the rise, with AI assistants—including Siri AI—now more capable and intelligent than ever.

Siri AI is already a big upgrade over the old Siri, but it’s getting even better in iOS 27.3.

As we reported last week, iOS 27.3 gives Siri AI many new capabilities across built-in Apple apps on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and more.

The one I’ve been testing the most is Apple Notes. Siri has offered basic Notes-related functionality for years, but it gains a whole new set of powers with the new update.

Here’s everything Siri told me it can do in Notes as of iOS 27.3:

That’s a lot of capabilities that can all now be handled by Siri.

I have nearly 3,000 notes saved in Apple Notes and use the app every day, so it’s been fun seeing what Siri can now do for me. One common example is that I’ve been able to have Siri save a link to the webpage I’m currently viewing inside a note, and even specify exactly where in the note I want it to go.

In theory, third-party notes apps may be able to offer similar controls sometime next year when app skills officially launch. For now though, anyone who wants to control their notes app by voice—or via Spotlight, as I tend to do on my iPad Pro—have another reason to use Apple Notes.

Have you tried Siri AI’s new Notes features in iOS 27.3? Let us know in the comments.

Now your little furry assistant can place calls on your behalf

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Meta’s Muse AI agent has emerged as one of the more recognizable digital personal assistants as of late.

It currently holds the #2 spot on the App Store among the top free apps category can definitely be attributed to its cute furry avatar, as well as what it can do for its users. Some of the best use cases involve automating job applications, building a site & online store via coding suggestions and handling a home insurance customer service call to get someone in touch with a human representative.

Speaking of that last case, Muse can be used to make phone calls on a user’s behalf to handle all sorts of assorted tasks. But what was once a feature only available to those with early access privileges has now become more widely available to those who are willing to pay up.

For those of you not in the know about Muse’s ability to make phone calls, here’s how it works.

🚨MUSE FEATURE ALERT!!!🚨 lots of you have been asking for this one… muse can make phone calls for you! ☎️📞📲 let muse take care of all those calls you don’t want to make. insurance? cable? DMV? dinner res? not your problem anymore. out now to paid subs in the US 🇺🇸 https://t.co/dsyMNmI2UbNovember 12, 2026

Paid subscription plans currently come in at $20/month for the “Power” tier (which comes with 500 million Muse tokens) and $100/month for the “Maximum” tier (which comes with three billion Muse tokens).

Among the sort of phone call chores Muse is promised to work with are making reservations, scheduling appointments, getting a human rep on the line at a company you’re paying bills to and more. Right now, Muse can only make phone calls to businesses in the US.

There have already been plenty of examples of Muse users taking advantage of its phone-calling capabilities and walking away with success stories from the whole ordeal. Last month, Moltbook creator and Meta Superintelligence employee Matt Schlicht hopped on X to detail how Muse helped him set up an appointment to get his car fixed:

My muse called Volvo for me to see when the next available appointment is. You can listen to the phone call here. I have it do multiple calls like this every day (I'm still trying to get better and better at leveraging muse). My muse called, waited on the line for 15 minutes, and then got the information I needed. - Saved me a ton of time - Muse was able to talk to the other person, with no confusion or interruptions on Volvo's side, and got the info we needed (This is the real transcript from the call but the audio has been recreated for this video)October 9, 2026

Making this Muse feature work for you is as simple as speaking to it through text or voice mode to contact a business for you in connection with a specific task.

Muse then works on its own to develop a plan that entails identifying the business it needs to call, finding the right phone number and choosing the right details to communicate to whoever is on the other end of the line during the call.

The agent goes on to dial the company, listens for automated phone responses and human greetings, makes its way through menu prompts and stays on hold for you. It’s worth pointing out that many businesses have chosen to hang up on Muse due to concerns over spam calls and general frustration with bots.

Muse is now among the growing group of AI assistants that can make phone calls on their own—that collective includes Genspark, Google (via a feature called “agenetic calling”), Instinct Concierge and CALL-E.

Time will tell if this feature becomes the norm for Muse users or even more of an annoyance for businesses who might decide to ignore all Muse calls altogether at some point.
