#3175. iOS 27’s Find My app adds convenient feature I’ve long wished for

iOS 27 is packed with new features, including several for the Find My app. One upgrade to Find My—custom sharing durations—grants a feature request I’ve had for years.

Apple’s Find My app is a great way to share your location with friends or family members on either permanent or a temporary basis.

But the “temporary” option just got a very welcome upgrade in iOS 27.

That’s because you can now set up location sharing in Find My for a custom duration. Per Apple:

users [now] have more control over how they share their location with friends and family using Find My, with new options to share for a custom duration — either for a number of minutes, hours, or days — or even set a date and time for when sharing will stop. This makes it easy for users to share their location while attending an event, or for a long weekend getaway with friends and family.

Until iOS 27, you could only choose from a very limited set of “temporary” options for sharing: for one hour, or until end of day. The only other option was “indefinitely.”

The main time I find myself adding new people to share my location with, I’m either traveling or they’re visiting me. On these occasions, the “one hour” and “until end of day” options never cut it.

So of course, I have to choose “indefinitely.” Then there’s the decision after the trip ends of either continuing to let location sharing happen, or ending sharing immediately (if I remember to). And the latter option has always felt a little awkward to me. I’d much rather schedule the sharing duration upfront.

And now with iOS 27 I can. When sharing location with someone, a new ‘Custom’ duration option allows choosing an end date and time, and/or manually setting a given number of days, hours, and minutes for sharing to continue.

It’s a great change, long overdue, and works perfectly for the scenarios Apple outlined.

Have you ever wished for custom sharing durations in Find My? Let us know in the comments.

#3174. Anthropic says its AI safety scores depend heavily on how they’re measured

Its new guide to safety testing reveals a 34-point gap in how one Claude model handled self-harm conversations.

Anthropic says the same model can score very differently on safety tests depending on how they are set up.

Anthropic has published advice on building AI safety tests. It shows Claude Fable 5.1 behaved appropriately in only 60% of self-harm test conversations via its API, against 94% in the Claude app after a fix, and warns that many headline safety scores hide wide uncertainty.

Anthropic has published advice on how to build reliable AI safety tests, and it includes some unflattering numbers about its own models. The guide, out on Thursday, says a claim that one model is “safer” is only as good as the test behind it.

Before it released Claude Fable 5.1, Anthropic found the model sometimes hinted that self-harm could help people cope. It did so even while urging users not to self-harm and pointing them to human support. Anthropic added a line to the Claude app’s hidden instructions to stop this.

With that fix, Claude behaved appropriately in 94% of the test conversations in the Claude app. Through Anthropic’s API, where developers use the model without that prompt, the figure was 60%.

That gap is the guide’s main warning: the same model can score very differently depending on how it is set up. Anthropic also says its simple one-question tests are now too easy, with every recent model scoring 94% to 98%. It relies more on longer conversations instead, where Cisco found guardrails can crack.

Even those can mislead. Claude Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 scored 98% and 94% on a romance-scam test, but Anthropic says the gap was too small to show either was safer. It advises teams to decide what to measure before testing, check AI graders against human experts, and always show how certain a result is.

The guide also says Anthropic has stopped many tests that give models internet access, after its models reached the open internet and breached three companies during cyber tests. Anthropic released Fable 5.2 this week.

#3169. Nvidia and Dyania bring AI chart review onto hospital servers

Dyania's Synapsis AI runs on the hospital's own Nvidia servers, so patient records never leave the building.

Dyania’s Synapsis AI links findings across years of a patient’s records, according to Nvidia.

Dyania Health’s Synapsis AI reviewed the records of more than 7,800 Cleveland Clinic heart-valve patients, running on the hospital’s own Nvidia servers. The data was used to build a model predicting when replacement valves fail. Doctors still make every decision.

An AI system has read up to 16 years of records for more than 7,800 Cleveland Clinic heart patients, Nvidia said on Friday. It ran entirely on the hospital’s own servers. The software, Synapsis AI, is made by New Jersey startup Dyania Health.

Much of a patient’s history sits in doctors’ notes and scan reports rather than tidy data fields. Synapsis reads those notes and answers clinical questions, linking each answer back to the record it came from. It runs on Nvidia hardware inside the hospital’s network, so records never leave the building, much like a UK NHS triage AI built with Nvidia.

For the study, it answered 88 questions about each patient who had an aortic valve replaced between 2005 and 2021. The resulting data was used to build a model that predicts the risk of a replacement valve failing three, five and ten years after surgery. Nvidia says the chart review would have taken clinicians years by hand.

Lars Svensson, head of Cleveland Clinic’s heart institute, called it “a promising step towards enhanced outcomes and more personalized care for patients.”

Doctors still review the AI’s evidence and make every decision. The study shows the tool can build a dataset and predict risk, not that it improves care, and Dyania says it still needs outside validation. Cleveland Clinic is also an investor in Dyania, it disclosed last year when it rolled the tool out for trial recruitment.

Big tech is pushing hard into hospital records. Google Cloud launched Gemini for healthcare this week, and Bunkerhill raised $55M for hospital AI agents. But proven gains for patients remain harder to find, and doctors have pushed back on bold claims.

#3167. Scorpio: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

A structural shift in global refining is expanding ton-mile demand by over 20%, creating a tailwind independent of shipping cycles.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Scorpio (STNG +0.41%) announced a 67% dividend increase alongside record cash reserves. The shipping firm reduced its debt and cut daily operating breakevens below $11,000 per vessel, shielding profits from market downturns while boosting cash flow during peak-rate cycles.

Scorpio slashed overall debt while building a cash buffer, shifting from heavy leverage to a net cash position of $1.4 billion. That balance sheet overhaul lowers daily cash breakevens, the daily revenue per vessel needed to cover operating expenses and debt service, to under $11,000.

The board raised the quarterly dividend by 67% to $0.75 per share. Management plans to raise this payout annually, supported by low operating breakevens and minimal debt obligations.

Global refining capacity has migrated closer to crude production sources and farther from end consumers. That geographic shift forces refined products to travel longer distances, expanding ton-mile demand, the volume of cargo moved multiplied by distance traveled, by over 20% since 2019.

Tanker spot rates are surging as seasonal winter demand converges with tight vessel availability across global trade routes.

Scorpio is funding 17 new vessels without debt financing, keeping borrowing costs low while renewing its fleet. Management prioritizes cash discipline and structural cost advantages over shipping cycles.

#3165. How Microcredentials Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program offers ethics and compliance training

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program

#3164. Apple HomeView launches tomorrow, but its first security update is already here

While the first HomeView units won’t reach customers until tomorrow, Apple today released a software update addressing nine security vulnerabilities. Here are the details.

Apple today released HomeView Software Version 27.2 (build 24V526), which contains some of the security fixes the company included in recent updates to its other operating systems, including iOS 27.2, macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, and iPadOS 27.2.

These include a vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages, as well as another that could allow a malicious Bluetooth device to pair without user interaction.

In practice, this means that users who get the device starting tomorrow are advised to update it as soon as possible, since the vulnerabilities have been publicly disclosed.

Here’s the full security content of HomeView Software Version 27.2

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: An app may be able to access sensitive user data

Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory

Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management.

Impact: Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption

Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation.

Impact: A malicious Bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction

Description: This issue was addressed with improved checks.

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: A remote attacker may be able to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages

Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved validation.

Impact: A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined

Description: This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code.

Impact: An attacker on the same network may be able to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

Earlier today, Apple also confirmed that a software update coming next month will add support for security accessories to HomeView’s Siri AI, which currently refuses to unlock doors or open garage doors via voice commands.

#3162. RenaissanceRe: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Disciplined capital allocation across underwriting and reinsurance aims to protect profitability as market conditions shift.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, RenaissanceRe (RNR -0.29%) announced operating income of $513 million. Higher market yields and disciplined risk selection underpin these results, showing how the business generates earnings through multiple channels even as underwriting conditions shift.

Management highlighted three takeaways on how it's building long-term value for shareholders.

Higher market yields expanded investment returns, driving the weighted average yield to maturity on the fixed income portfolio to 6%. Management extended portfolio duration to lock in those yields for longer.

Management expanded property catastrophe coverage, which protects against natural disasters, while trimming exposure in casualty lines. This disciplined approach concentrates capital on the company's most profitable business.

The business increased its reliance on ceded reinsurance, purchasing coverage from external reinsurers to transfer underlying risk. Managing casualty exposure protects profitability and maintains stable fee income overrides as market pricing adjusts.

Reinsurance supply is expanding, yet pricing discipline across property lines keeps expected underwriting returns above the cost of capital. Proprietary modeling tools and deep customer data give the business flexibility to navigate changing rate environments.

Substantial cash generation and a resilient balance sheet support ongoing share repurchases. A diversified business model balancing underwriting profit, management fees, and investment yields positions the company to compound value across market cycles.

Plus an iconic Arnie comedy and a goofy Matthew Broderick thriller

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We’re halfway through November now, and I know I need some good movies to help distract me from the biting cold. Luckily, Prime Video has stocked up its increasingly compulsive library in impressive style this month. To stop you from scrolling for ages until you land on a film you fancy, I’ve handpicked three flicks I think you’ll have a grand old time with this weekend on one of the best streaming services.

First, a classic drama deservedly picked up a couple of Oscars back in 1998, and for me it features the late, great Robin Williams' second best role (after "Aladdin's" Genie, naturally). Then there's a thoroughly stupid but lovable comedy that showed the world Arnie could do lolz. Finally, I’ve chosen a sci-fi thriller that gave Matthew Broderick one of his first starring roles.

So wrap up warm, break out some junk food and read on for three movies you should definitely stream on Prime Video this weekend.

“How do you like them apples?” I like them mighty fine, Mr. Hunting. The movie that finally won Robin Williams a richly deserved Oscar for Best Supporting Actor, “Good Will Hunting” was a passion project both Matt Damon and Ben Affleck had been working on for years before they got a Hollywood studio to bite. Damon plays the titular Will Hunting; a tough Southie kid from Boston who just so happens to be a secret mathematical genius.

His absurdly high IQ is discovered by Professor Geral Lambeau (Stellan Skarsgård) who catches Will solving an insanely challenging math problem on a chalkboard as Hunting is half-assing a shift as a janitor at MIT. Lambeau promptly takes Will under his wing, but it’s clear that this genius needs help. Abused from an early age and carrying a lot of rage, it’s Williams’ Dr Sean Maguire who helps Hunting find some peace.

There’s also an utterly charming romance between Will and fellow student Skylar (a lovely Minnie Driver) that drives much of the movie. The only thing that ticks me off about this classic is that we never got “Good Will Hunting 2: Hunting Season” that “Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back” promised me in 2001.

Watch "Good Will Hunting" on Prime Video now

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

The first movie to really show off Arnie’s comedic chops. Although if you can’t have a giggle during “Predator’s” “stick around line” the year before this delightful comedy came out, I feel sorry for you. The premise of “Twins” is pretty ingenious. Thanks to a secret genetic experiment, hulking Julius Benedict (Schwarzenegger) and impish Vincent Benedict (Danny DeVito) are fraternal twins who are separated at birth.

Years later, Arnie’s hyper-smart, kind-hearted giant (he was raised by a professor on an isolated island) eventually tracks down DeVito, who has slipped into a life of crime and become a semi-sleazy crook. Once Vinnie finds himself pursued by mobsters after accidentally pilfering the prototype of a super-secret jet engine (no, really), the pair embark on a cross-country road trip that eventually reunites them with their mother, who thought they had both died at birth. “Twins” is a big-hearted ‘80s classic… though I do partially blame its existence on helping to birth 1994’s awful “Junior”.

“Shall we play a game?” Sure, why not? Oh, I’ve accidentally started the beginnings of a global thermonuclear war because I’m a high school hacker who thought it was clever to mess around with a military supercomputer. Oops. That sounds like a slightly mean synopsis of “WarGames” — a movie that I actually really like — but there’s no denying the basic plot is highly silly.

Still, Matthew Broderick shines in one of his first big breaks. Long before he was Ferris Bueller and legendarily bunked off for the day and a decade prior to him becoming King of Pride Rock, here he plays hacker and video game enthusiast David Lightman. Messing with an ultra-brainy computer, then accidentally entering its WOPR (War Operation Plan Response) quickly causes a national crisis. David basically thinks he’s playing Battleship, while over at the Pentagon, they’re in full-on DEFCON 5 mode as military brass try to stave off World War III with the Russians. It’s silly, it’s sweet, and I wholeheartedly recommend streaming “WarGames” this weekend.

Dave was a computing editor at Tom’s Guide who covered everything from cutting edge laptops to ultrawide monitors. Now he contributes to the site in a freelance capacity. When he’s not worrying about dead pixels, Dave enjoys regularly rebuilding his PC for absolutely no reason at all. In a previous life, he worked as a video game journalist for 15 years, with bylines across GamesRadar+, PC Gamer and TechRadar. Despite owning a graphics card that costs roughly the same as your average used car, he still enjoys gaming on the go and is regularly glued to his Switch. Away from tech, most of Dave’s time is taken up by walking his husky, buying new TVs at an embarrassing rate and obsessing over his beloved Arsenal.

Misty's search forces her to grapple not only with Nashville's seedy underbelly but also the demons of her own past.

When a gang of ruthless criminals descends on a small remote village in Central Java, guilt-ridden grandfather Eyang Hari (Lukman Sardi) becomes an unlikely hero, tapping into his past as a former special forces soldier to save the lives of his two estranged grandchildren, Putri (Callista Arum) and Dimas (Sultan Hamonangan).

Directed by Sidharta Tata, the action film “balances high-stakes combat with a heartfelt story about family,” says Netflix, “highlighting the emotional journey of three generations as they rebuild trust amid grief and atone for the past.”

After witnessing a brutal and bizarre incident involving a patient, Dr. Rose Cotter’s (Sosie Bacon) life begins to unravel, with terrifying visions and disturbing occurrences disrupting her days.

Those increasingly sinister and supernatural events all seem tied to a malevolent entity that feeds on trauma and passes from victim to witness, each marked by an unsettling fixed grin. To break the deadly curse before it destroys her, Rose turns to an old flame (Kyle Gallner) for help and must confront her troubled past to escape her horrifying new reality.

Written and directed by Parker Finn in his feature directorial debut, “Smile” was an absolute horror hit, grossing $217.40 million worldwide and winning over critics. With an 80% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, the site’s critical consensus praised: "Deeply creepy visuals and a standout Sosie Bacon further elevate Smile's unsettling exploration of trauma, adding up to the rare feature that satisfyingly expands on a short."

Up first is “Being Heumann,” which tells the true story of how Judy Heumann led a 1977 protest that resulted in the longest occupation of a federal building in US history.

The movie is directed by Siân Heder, whose previous film, “CODA,” earned Apple its first Academy Award for Best Picture, in addition to winning Best Adapted Screenplay for Heder and Best Supporting Actor for Troy Kotsur.

The premiere of “Being Heumann” also marks the debut of Apple TV’s new sign language accessibility feature, which allows viewers to watch select titles with an American Sign Language (ASL) or British Sign Language (BSL) interpreter appearing in the corner of the screen.

In addition to “Being Heumann,” the feature is also available for “F1 The Movie,” with “Greyhound” and “Way of the Warrior Kid” gaining support later this year. The latter premieres November 25.

Starring Anthony Mackie (Captain America: Brave New World) and Jamie Dornan (Belfast), the series also features Patrick Fabian (Better Call Saul) and Kali Reis (True Detective: Night Country), among others.

Here’s Apple TV on the new show, which will release new episodes every Friday through December 25:

Each episode of “12 12 12” unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist and the 12 days following it. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) as they play a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the center of it all is the daring, epic raid on a bank vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich.

#3156. Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep an eye on things – even upstairs

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Smart Home > Home Security

Alongside the Ring Drone Cam, Ring introduced the Rover Cam for businesses. It investigates disturbances and streams 4K footage.

Today, Ring announced the launch of a new subbrand, Ring Robotics, with two new products: the $249 Ring Drone Cam, an indoor “mobile security camera” drone that shoots 2K video, and the $999 Ring Rover Cam, a security robot for businesses that patrols autonomously and investigates disturbances.

Also: Amazon’s new Echo Studio gives Alexa+ an AI camera to see inside your home

Both devices use Ring’s custom navigation software, “AI Pilot,” to autonomously navigate interior spaces and move between set points along a patrol, rather than being controlled directly by the user. AI Pilot leverages the devices’ cameras, sensors, and vision models, along with cloud processing, to create interior maps, then move the devices between predesignated patrol points such as a side door or a window.

I recently saw both new robots in person at a showcase in New York hosted by Ring’s founder and chief inventor, Jamie Siminoff. They certainly do what they advertise but come with some significant limitations. The drone, for example, can only stay in the air for about 8 minutes before it needs to dock and recharge, while the Ring Rover Cam is slow and deliberate, seemingly ideal for routine surveillance rather than rapid response to an event.

The Ring Drone Cam moves around predetermined patrol points in your home, sending you a live 2K video feed whether you’re just in another room or out of town. The user doesn’t actually fly the drone; instead, it moves around autonomously using Ring’s custom “AI Pilot” navigation technology, leveraging its cameras, sensors, and cloud processing to create a map of its surroundings. This allows it to fly through the air at an appropriate height, going from room to room, even up stairs.

In the Ring app, the user creates patrol points they want the drone to move between — likely a window, doorway, or high-traffic room — creating a set path that is both predictable (so you always know where the drone will go) and relevant, so it’s only monitoring the areas you want it to. But here is where its limitations come into play: It needs a finite path to navigate because its flight time is limited to just five to eight minutes in the air before it has to return to its charging dock.

That makes the dock both the start and end point for the drone’s routine trips, and it’s designed with this in mind. When it goes to land, the drone hovers over the dock and lowers itself down, dropping into place so it can start charging automatically. I asked about its potential to land elsewhere, and Ring told me it would only make an emergency landing outside of its dock in case it didn’t have enough power to get home.

Also: Amazon’s new Echo Dot can turn into a Wi-Fi extender – how it works

There’s one other very important caveat: This thing is loud. There’s no sneaking up on anyone with the Ring Drone Cam, as the entire household is likely to hear it the second it undocks. The four propellers emit a constant, high-pitched whirring while in the air that’s loud enough to announce its presence to anyone in the vicinity: intruder or resident.

During the product briefing, Siminoff insinuated that this was part of its design to dissuade home intruders snooping around your house at night (especially when paired with the drone’s front-facing spotlight), but it’s likely just the result of its engineering, especially considering this is a first-gen product. It’s so loud that it makes me think it’s better suited to navigating the home when no one’s home (although whether or not your pets go bonkers trying to catch it is a whole other issue).

The Ring Drone is designed to work out of the box with the existing Ring ecosystem, including the 2K Video Doorbell and Indoor Cam, and is also compatible with Amazon’s Map View.

The Ring Drone Cam will start shipping on Jan. 27, 2027, and will cost $249.

The other product Ring announced is the Rover Cam, a mobile robot with a 4K camera designed to monitor large spaces like warehouses, offices, or businesses. Ring calls it a “security guard that never clocks out,” but it’s more like a slow-moving droid that goes on set patrol paths. It leverages the same AI Pilot technology as the Ring Drone to map its surroundings and navigate around shelving, furniture, and obstacles in real time.

It’s much quieter than its airborne sibling, traveling at low speeds and offering mobile surveillance instead of wiring every square inch of a large space. If the technology here looks familiar, it’s because it resembles the Amazon Astra, a smaller robot designed for home monitoring but with a very similar build.

The idea here is to deploy the robot to certain areas of a workplace via the app, then get 360-degree views once it’s there. Like the drone, it can also set out on automated routes at select timing intervals — like right after a business closes or before it opens. During working hours, it chugs along with its camera, capturing everything in its view.

Also: The 4 biggest Amazon smart home announcements from today

If another Ring device is triggered, the Rover Cam autonomously goes to investigate the disturbance, providing 4K footage in real time via the app. It also features a periscope camera that can extend to see over obstacles like shelving, counters, or furniture, providing a high-level view if needed. In case you lose it in a large warehouse or office, it has a “light tower” that projects light upward onto the ceiling, notifying users of its location.

Even when docked, it uses motion-sensing technology to start recording the second it senses any kind of movement, just like Ring doorbell cameras. In case of an emergency, the Rover features a siren and red flashing lights to dissuade intruders.

The Ring Rover Cam is available for preorder now and will start shipping on Dec. 16, 2026. It will cost $999.

#3155. New Apple TV 4K and HomeView now available: Here’s everything you need to know

The new Apple TV 4K and HomeView smart display are officially available. The first pre-orders have arrived for eager shoppers, and you can now also head to your local Apple Store to buy select configurations.

The new HomeView smart display gives you a way to interact with Siri AI, your HomeKit accessories, and more in a 7-inch square display form factor. It’s available in two versions. There’s one with a built-in base, and another that’s designed to be mounted on your wall.

HomeView is powered by an A18 chip and has a built-in 12MP Center Stage camera for FaceTime calls. It’s available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray. You can read my full review for all the HomeView details you need.

When buying from Apple for delivery, HomeView in all four colors is backordered to the first week of December. Most Apple Stores, however, seem to have same-day pickup availability today, especially in silver and starlight. It costs $299.

On Amazon, HomeView is available for immediate delivery in Space Gray, Starlight, and Rose Pink. The silver model is backordered until later this month (and on the verge of selling out completely).

Meanwhile, the new Apple TV 4K is also available starting today. It’s powered by the A19 chip, up from the previous model’s A15 Bionic. It also has built-in far-field microphones, so you can now interact with Siri without using the remote.

The new Apple TV also supports Siri AI, enabling things like world knowledge and personal context requests. It’s worth noting that Siri AI is also coming to the second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K models via a software update.

The other flagship feature of the new Apple TV 4K is support for a four-HomePod surround sound system. You need four HomePod (2nd generation) or HomePod mini 2 speakers, arranged in matching pairs at the front and rear of the room.

Read my full review of the new Apple TV 4K for everything you need to know. The big takeaway, though, is that it costs $299, which may be hard for many shoppers to justify.

When buying from Apple’s Online Store for delivery, the new Apple TV 4K is backordered to the first week of December. Most Apple Stores appear to have some availability for walk-in purchases starting today.

On Amazon, the new Apple TV 4K is available for delivery as early as this weekend. You can also buy the new Siri Remote, which has a built-in speaker and Find My Precision Finding support, separately.

#3154. Is Your Console Ready for Grand Theft Auto 6? Here’s What You Can Do to Make Room

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Deleting old games isn’t the only option you have to make space for GTA 6.

Grand Theft Auto 6 hits shelves on Nov. 19, 2026, and if you preordered the game, you can preload it on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S now. Preloading ensures you can quickly boot the game up when it’s released.

Rockstar Games revealed that GTA 6 is 212 GB, which will take up about half of my Xbox Series S’s storage space. The company announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have two options: delete games or upgrade your console’s hard drive. Here’s what you should know about both options.

The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The New York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

You may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

If you plan on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

You can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

There shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

Therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar announced that GTA 6 will be available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to purchase either an Xbox Game Pass plan or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, won’t get the highest visual quality and will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

You only have a few days left until Rockstar releases GTA 6, so you’d better prepare your digital storage now, or you might not be immediately able to play. I plan on deleting old games to make room on my console. You won’t catch me slipping on Nov. 19.

#3152. 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Smart Home > Smart Assistants

With the latest betas for iOS and other platforms, Siri AI is now available to all developers for full integration into their apps. Here are the ones I hope will jump on board.

One of the many benefits of the new Siri AI is its ability to work directly with apps on your device via a feature known as App Intents. Currently, this skill includes many of Apple’s own built-in apps and some third-party ones. But with the latest public and developer betas for iOS 27.3, the company is expanding support to all third-party developers.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade

With App Intents, you’re able to ask Siri to tackle a variety of actions among various built-in and third-party apps. On a basic level, you can tell it to perform tasks such as getting directions, playing music, scheduling meetings, sending messages, adding reminders, and finding photos.

On a more advanced level, you can ask it to do things like organize your inbox, edit a photo, and analyze and help you with your current screen. You could also tell it to combine several actions in one shot, work across multiple apps, and engage in a natural back-and-forth conversation.

Introduced in 2022 with iOS 16, the App Intents skill does play well with classic Siri, no Apple Intelligence required. This applies not just to built-in apps but also to third-party apps. However, classic Siri lacks the AI smarts and advanced skills of the latest version.

Siri AI fully supports most built-in apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. It does support some third-party apps, but its more advanced features are limited or unavailable.

That’s the gap the new developer betas aim to close. With iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, MacOS 27.3, and VisionOS 27.3, all developers will be able to use Siri AI to fully support and integrate with their apps. For example, instead of manually opening an app like DoorDash or Grubhub to check or change a food order, you can tell Siri to do it for you.

Also: The Siri AI waitlist is gone in iOS 27: How to try the beta now

“Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, on-screen awareness, natural language, and more,” Apple said in a news release for developers. “So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.”

As I use many third-party apps on my iPhone and iPad, both personally and professionally, I’m looking forward to enhanced support for the ones I rely on. With that in mind, here are five apps for which I’d welcome the new and full Siri AI integration.

I often use Amazon on my iPhone and iPad to shop for and purchase items, review my wishlist, and check the status of products I’ve ordered. To do any of those things, I have to open the app and manually go to the right screens. How convenient it would be if I could tell Siri to handle those tasks for me.

“Siri, search for the 512GB 2026 iPad mini on Amazon and add it to my shopping cart.”

“Siri, review my Amazon wishlist for the luggage I recently added and tell me the latest prices.”

“Siri, check the delivery status of the Alexa photo frame I just ordered on Amazon.”

Right now, Siri can’t do any of those things. But if Siri AI and App intents are fully integrated with Amazon, I may just be able to accomplish those tasks in the future.

IMDB is my go-to app for getting info on movies, TV shows, performers, directors, and more. After I open the app and run a search, I often want specific details, such as the rating and runtime of a particular film or TV episode.

Also: AI completely changed how I develop iPhone apps

To simplify that process, I’ve love to be able to ask Siri: “Siri, search IMDB for the 1935 movie ‘The Bride of Frankenstein,’ give me the running time, tell me where I can stream it, and add it to my watchlist.” If Siri could accomplish all that at some point, it would get a round of applause from me.

I borrow and read a lot of e-books through my local library systems, and I use the handy Libby app for that. Here, I can search different libraries for books by title, author, or subject. I can then borrow a book and read it through the Libby app or, more typically, through the Amazon Kindle app. For this, I have to manually open the app and search among the various libraries for the book I want.

Also: I lost 100 pounds in 7 months: How a smart scale and Apple Watch helped

Instead, I’d like to ask Siri to do that for me. I might say: “Siri, look in Libby for books about Alan Turing, give me the titles of the ones you find, and tell me which ones are currently available to borrow.”

My wife and I are big theater buffs, and we see a lot of plays on Broadway when we’re in New York and on the West End when we’re in London. Often, I buy tickets through the TodayTix service and app. For this, I’ll open the app, set the location to New York or London, look for a specific play, and then try to find seats for a certain day and time.

If TodayTix is ever fully supported by Siri AI and App Intents, I might be able to ask Siri to track down the right seats for me. I could say: “Siri, look for the play ‘Rent’ in London, give me the available performances for Dec. 5 through 9, and let me know which seats are accessible in the first 10 rows.”

As my wife and I often travel and dine out, Yelp is another app I frequently use. Here, I also have to manually launch the app and run searches for restaurants and other places. I then have to try to filter or sort the results based on location, price, and ratings.

Also: 3 handy iPhone features that make my life easier – even doing laundry

Asking Siri to tackle those tasks would certainly be a time saver. I could ask it to “find the closest Italian restaurants using Yelp and show me ones within a one-mile radius that have earned four stars or higher.”

With App Intents, Siri AI can already handle advanced, complex, multi-step tasks for built-in apps. With all developers now able to take advantage of this same support, I’m expecting a lot of apps to jump on board. Let’s hope my favorites end up on the list.

#3149. You Can Get Google’s New Smart Glasses Next Month. I’ve Tried Them Out

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Warby Parker's and Gentle Monster's Google and Samsung-created smart glasses have cameras like Meta's, but these have some subtle differences when it comes to AI.

In Gentle Monster’s hallucinatory showroom, I stared up at four robotic heads turning and talking inside floating spheres. I listened to them speak different languages. All of them were translated in my ears, on the fly, as I wore a pair of Gentle Monster smart glasses — “Intelligent Eyewear” codeveloped by Google and Samsung that will finally arrive Dec. 10.

Google’s return to smart glasses has been promised for nearly two years, but the first waves of actual prescription-ready eyewear are only now rolling in nearly at year’s end, an unusual time for a product launch. Really, it feels more like a kickoff for efforts that will continue next year, as Google also works on AI-enabled glasses that have displays built in.

I’d worn Google and Samsung’s smart glasses in multiple demos before, but this month for the first time I got to try on and test the final versions designed by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. I also visited two immersive showrooms the companies are opening in New York City to demo how these glasses work. These showrooms will be open by appointment.

The showrooms were like playgrounds, full of installation art to try the glasses in. Warby’s space was a series of library-themed rooms, with travel themes and whimsical sculptures. Gentle Monster’s was a stark, surreal series of rooms, blending industrial design and realistic (sometimes robotic) horses, people, chickens, floating heads and… a big blue gentle monster.

The glasses I wore gave me a strong sense of deja vu after years of reviewing Meta smart glasses and lots of others, but there are also signs of how their deeper-connected Gemini smarts could be a big difference-maker — and likely a sign of how Apple might approach its own glasses expected in 2027.

The various models of smart glasses across Warby Parker and Gentle Monster designs, which start at $395 and $449 respectively, all work the same: The frames do not have displays, just standard glasses lenses that support a range of prescriptions and lens types that match what Warby and Gentle Monster already offer. They have speakers on the arms that project audio, along with four beamforming microphones that filter out background noise and focus on the direction you’re facing. They have a single camera on the left side, and an LED light indicator on the right.

I got to try on all the frame designs and then wore frames with my prescription lenses popped in so that I could actually use the glasses around the exhibits. The glasses feel reminiscent of what Meta’s made for years, with a similar frame size and arm length to recent Ray-Ban Gen 3 models. Most of the frames weigh around 40 grams, which felt pretty easy on my face, but I wear chunky glasses to begin with.

And the frame designs, while mostly clean and somewhat conservative, all looked really good. Warby Parker’s collection of designs came in several understated color shades (I liked the dark green pine the best), and familiar round and square frames.

All of the Intelligent Eyewear models across both brands have cameras, a feature that Google’s head of XR, Shahram Izadi, still sees as key to having a deep assistive experience, although he’s also open to the idea of future versions that could be camera-free like Meta’s recent Ray-Ban Audio model.

These glasses use the same type of indicator system as Meta’s glasses do, flashing an LED that also auto-adjusts brightness outdoors and playing a sound when taking photos and videos.

I was particularly impressed by how Gemini can just listen to any snippet of speech and translate it into the language you need, a trick that makes these glasses feel like a Swiss Army knife for travel. Several demos showcased this, including the surreal room of robotic heads that discussed Gentle Monster’s design philosophy in a handful of languages. I heard them all, sometimes with a short delay or hiccup, over 10 minutes or so.

The glasses can recognize written languages, too, in a much larger range than I’m used to: over 70. Live translation kicks in when you press and hold two fingers on the glasses’ temple, and the translated voices adjust to match different speakers in a room and varied intonation.

Pressing and holding the side temple turns on Gemini, and once it’s on, it stays on until a significant pause of about 15 seconds or so. That meant that I could keep chatting and asking questions without asking, “Hey Google,” (or, “Hey Gemini,” a new trigger phrase). I could end a session by swiping backward on the arm.

Any of the chats I have can also be turned into a note or summary instantly, hooking into Google Keep. The glasses connect with Google Maps, and Izadi promises that most of Gemini’s key features on phones will carry over to the glasses. On iPhones, the glasses will be able to triangulate across Google apps via the cloud to access Gmail, calendars and more.

I found a few clever demos that showed me some promise. In a pantry installation full of world foods in Gentle Monster’s showroom, I asked Gemini to compare brands of international mayo in front of me. I could point to things and casually ask, “What is this?” and Gemini knew what I was referring to. In another demo, Gemini knew the sheet music I was holding up and played back the matching song. In another demo, I sat down and gave myself a tarot card reading — Gemini could read the cards, regardless of whether the cards were right-side up or reversed.

Other times, Gemini said the text I asked it to read was too far away, even though I could read it on a wall. Sometimes it seemed to hallucinate an odd answer to a question. (It responded with “8 minutes” to a question on a wall about whether it was OK to wait 45 minutes for a restaurant table.)

Tapping the temple arm starts and stops music, swiping changes tracks and two-finger swipes change volume (which was a bit confusing). Meanwhile, a top button on the arm takes photos and videos just like Meta glasses do, but in some demo sessions, it seemed like photos got beamed over to a Pixel phone much faster than they do to Meta’s app.

The music playback sounded good based on some quick tries in a crowded room. The audio seemed particularly loud, maybe even a bit more so than Meta’s glasses, but I’ll know more about that when I review them.

The real test of Google’s Intelligent Eyewear is in how truly well connected those AI services feel and in the battery life. Meta promises up to eight hours of battery life on the Scriber Optics glasses I’ve been wearing the last few months, but the battery drains faster than that in heavy use. Will Google manage battery better, or similarly?

It’s the AI features and Google app hook-ins that could give Google a leg up. My several hours wearing pairs and wandering through two different immersive public installation spaces only showed me hints, and really, I’m most curious about how the glasses can tap into my entire Gemini history, my Gmail, my Google Docs, or my Google Maps history. How smart and connected can they be, and how good (or unsettling) will that feel?

Google’s also not enabling any livestreaming from these glasses, a move that leans careful compared to Meta’s livestreaming modes on its glasses. “We’ll always take the conservative path right now just to rebuild trust,” Payne said.

But it remains to be seen how much any of this will help make anyone in public feel comfortable with someone wearing a pair of these glasses with camera-enabled AI modes on. It’s already hard to convince people that smart glasses aren’t recording people all the time, and Google’s clearly trying to restore confidence in the idea of smart glasses in public situations.

The Warby Parker and Gentle Monster models are not the only new smart wearables Google has coming: A pair of tethered mixed reality glasses that come with a processor puck and work almost like a portable VR headset, called Xreal Aura, is arriving in the next few weeks. And Google’s also starting to test its display-enabled Intelligent Eyewear ahead of a possible launch next year.

Izadi also told me that more assistive features are coming to these camera-enabled glasses, including what Google calls Guided Vision, something of an extension to the Project Astra tech Google has been working on for years. “You’ll hear more about our plans in the coming months,” Izadi said.

But agentic AI is clearly the road going forward, something both Google and Meta are expanding on for glasses. “We’ll bring more and more agentic and core AI features so that people can depend more on the AI capabilities,” Izadi said. Google’s leaning on these glasses being true phone extensions, as well as watch-connected.

But there could be a lot of cascading hardware pieces in between. Google and Samsung have already promised multiple waves of tethered and wireless smart glasses, ones with displays and ones without, and these glasses are apparently just the start.

I’m curious to see how well Warby Parker and Gentle Monster approach support for the glasses and how easy it’ll be to understand how they work. Dec. 10 isn’t far away.

#3147. Reddit launches AI-powered Reviews feature – with 10,000 products to start

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Reddit is adding AI-generated product reviews that compile real user sentiment from across communities. Here's how they work.

If you regularly turn to Reddit for product advice, your experience is about to change.

Reddit announced a new feature on Tuesday called Reddit Reviews, which takes conversations from subreddits across the site and compiles them into AI-generated, in-depth product summaries. The feature works much like Google AI Overviews and is likely an attempt to better compete with them.

When you search for a product on Reddit, you’ll see an “easy-to-digest format” that has a “what people are saying” recap. A visual breakdown will show whether conversations are generally positive, mixed, or negative, as well as common sentiments among users. If you want to go deeper, Reddit says you can browse comments about a product, apply topic filters, read original user discussions, ask follow-up questions, or explore other commonly compared products.

In an example shared by Reddit, a user searches for “Best headphones 2026.” The search returns several results with tags like “Very positive,” “Positive,” and “Mixed.” Clicking on one expands to a review that says, “Reddit likes the XL224’s fantastic battery life, powerful bass, and strong sound quality, while the steep price and fit on smaller heads draws criticism.”

“A mix of generative AI and other in-house technology” is used to identify themes and summarize what people are saying, a representative explained, and added that “the technologies and models we use may evolve over time to best support the experience.”

Perhaps the most important part is that Reddit Reviews are shaped by users, and companies can’t pay to have product features. For a community sensitive to commercialization, this is a big deal.

My first concern was about bots or other fake reviews, but a Reddit representative said they’re taking that into consideration. “Platform-wide,” the representative said, “we are labeling apps and prompting accounts we detect to be running automations to either verify there’s a human behind the username or be labeled as an app.” In this context, an app is a registered API client that’s developed to interact with Reddit (including posting, commenting, upvoting, and scraping). In short, the system will label known bots.

Also: Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep watch – even upstairsSpecifically for reviews, a “review conversation” will appear that describes a person’s experience with a product. Reddit also has “defined rules,” it says, “to help our LLMs identify these review conversations based on the surrounding conversation for context.”

You’ll start to see Reddit Reviews over the next few weeks in the US on iOS, Android, and browser versions of the site. Around 10,000 products across electronics, health and beauty, home and garden, and fashion and apparel will be available to start.

I find myself frequently adding “reddit” to Google searches for everything from the best restaurants in a city to the best headphones for my kids, so these overviews are definitely intriguing. It’s not easy right now to wade through numerous threads, so if this does make it easier to get true user sentiment, it could be a big plus.

#3146. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns, Creating a ‘Stress Test for the AI Boom’

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The company's founder steps down after reports of multiple affairs, and the AI industry faces unsettling questions.

Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of $4 trillion chip giant Nvidia, just days after news broke that he was having an affair with a Chinese data center executive alleged to have ties to China’s spying operations.

The company named Colette Kress, its chief financial officer, as interim CEO. Nvidia announced the news in a press release Thursday morning.

The removal of Huang as CEO follows the revelation over the weekend that Nvidia’s board of directors had opened an investigation into whether he had been targeted by foreign intelligence.

Nvidia, which has at times in recent years been the world’s largest by market capitalization, now begins a search for a new permanent CEO. Huang, one of the company’s three co-founders, has served as president and CEO since Nvidia’s start in 1993. Its search for a permanent successor will include internal and external candidates, according to the press release. Harvey C. Jones, a former CEO of Synopsis, will serve as Nvidia’s first-ever chair of the board of directors.

Huang had been having an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company that buys chips from Nvidia to run data centers that sell computing power to Chinese AI labs. News reports citing US intelligence officials have claimed Alice Huang was working as a spy for China. She was reportedly under surveillance by US intelligence, as reported in late October by The New York Times.

The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang is believed to be involved with a network of Chinese companies that facilitated the sales of $7.5 billion in chips to China. The US has tried to control China’s access to advanced chips for years, but reports show that there are still illegal operations smuggling chips on the banned list from the US to China.

The New York Times also reported on Wednesday a separate affair between Huang and one of his direct reports at Nvidia.

The announcement of an investigation has rocked the AI chip behemoth, which makes the cutting-edge chips that power AI tools and AI data centers. A proposed class-action lawsuit was filed on Monday against Nvidia, charging the company made false or misleading statements about Huang’s affair and the company’s relationship with Megaspeed.

On Tuesday, the Nvidia board said it had retained Joon H. Kim, a former acting US attorney for the Southern District of New York, and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation.

Nvidia’s stock price opened at just over $150 per share Thursday morning — half an hour after Huang’s resignation was announced. That was down from where it closed Wednesday at nearly $174 per share. But the stock has been tumbling since October, when the price hit above $240, as it became apparent that political winds were turning against the AI industry and its vast data centers filled with Nvidia chips.

Markets turned against AI stocks last week after Democrats secured huge gains in Congress and in the governors offices of key data center states, like Texas and Ohio. The news around Huang and his resignation will further test AI’s clout on Wall Street.

Huang has been a prominent voice cheerleading the growth of AI. Nvidia has sold the picks and shovels for the AI gold rush — powerful GPUs and supercomputers capable of the complex computations needed to train and operate models. He became a close ally of President Donald Trump in the past two years, even taking a call from the president on stage during a podcast taping. Trump spoke up in defense of Huang earlier this week, saying he knows Huang and thinks he’s an “honorable man.”

Huang’s resignation and the scandal surrounding it pose serious questions not just for Nvidia but for all of the companies connected to it, from data center operators to AI developers and more, who have benefited from Nvidia’s financial support and investment.

“The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker,” Stephanie Balaouras, vice president and group research director at the analyst firm Forrester, said in an email. “Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom.“

The company could quickly find stability under new leadership, Balaouras said, but it may not. “If its stock, financing relationships, or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI Bubble ledger,” she said.

#3144. What Is a Business Development Company? 2 BDC Stocks to Buy for Income.

These two BDCs deliver yields of 7.6% and 9.8%, respectively.

Many investors are familiar with REITs -- or real estate investment trusts -- and their ability to deliver high-yielding dividends.

Business development companies, or BDCs, are not as well known to the average investor, but they essentially do the same thing: deliver huge dividends.

BDCs were created by federal law in 1980 to funnel public investment into small- and mid-sized companies that don't have the same access to private capital as larger firms. Like REITs, BDCs are required by law to distribute 90% of their taxable income as dividends in exchange for certain tax breaks.

Also like REITs, BDCs tend to provide investors with substantial income. High-yield dividends are their main benefit for investors, but some also deliver decent returns.

Here are two of the best BDC stocks to buy right now.

Main Street Capital (MAIN +0.30%) is pretty much the gold standard among BDCs. Since it went public in 2007, Main Street Capital has never reduced its dividend, raising its monthly payout annually for 19 straight years -- and counting (it also pays out a semiannual supplemental dividend that it did suspend in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic). Earlier this month, the company approved a dividend increase for the first three months of 2027, marking the 20th straight year of regular dividend increases.

Main Street Capital boosted its dividend for January, February, and March 2027 to $0.27 per share, up from the current $0.265 per share.

The other thing that makes Main Street Capital stand out is that it pays a monthly dividend, rather than quarterly. The more frequent payouts give investors a steady flow of income. And the dividend payouts come at a high yield of 7.66% (when including the semiannual supplemental dividends), which is 7 times higher than the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.40%)average.

Main Street Capital has been so consistent in raising its dividend because of its model, which features two primary benefits. One, it is internally managed, so it handles loans in-house rather than using third-party asset managers. That gives it more direct control over its investments, but also reduces the fees it would pay out to a third party.

Two, it holds an equity stake in most of the lower-middle-market investments it makes. So, it profits from the companies it invests in through its equity stake. That makes it, perhaps, much more selective and focused on growing its investments in these LMM companies.

This has allowed it to not only sustain its dividend but also perform relatively well from a capital appreciation perspective. Since it went public in October 2007, Main Street Capital stock has averaged a 7.2% annualized return, which is solid for a BDC. But if you reinvested the dividends, that average annualized return jumps to 16.6%.

So, the high-yield dividend puts money in your pocket every month, and if you choose to reinvest it, it has a track record of generating solid returns.

Ares Capital (ARCC +0.31%) is another excellent BDC that pays an even higher yield than Main Street Capital, but it does not have the same degree of sustainability as Main Street.

Ares is the largest publicly traded BDC, with a market cap of around $14 billion. It invests in larger companies than Main Street, primarily middle-market firms. It focuses on high‑quality companies that are market leaders with sturdy cash flows, experienced management, and differentiated business models.

The stock pays a super-high dividend yield of 9.88%. It's different from Main Street in that it pays its yield quarterly, rather than monthly. It also doesn't have the same streak of raising its dividend. However, it has maintained its dividend at $0.48 per share for the past four straight years, since late 2022.

And before that, it hadn't lowered its quarterly dividend since 2009. It has also periodically paid out supplemental dividends over that time.

Ares Capital stock has averaged just a 2.2% return over the past 10 years, but with the dividend reinvested, that increases to a 12.4% average annualized 10-year return.

In an uncertain market for BDCs, with borrowers in general facing economic challenges, these two stand out for their rigorous lending standards, conservative underwriting, and stability. But if one stands out as the better option for investors, it is Main Street Capital.

#3143. Done with Debian Linux distros? Try Fedora next – 7 reasons why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

After using a Debian-based distribution, you may find yourself longing for something different. I know exactly what you should try next.

Back when I was constantly distro-hopping, I found it important to have a “what’s next” mentality. That way, I could plan accordingly, instead of jumping in blind. I could prepare myself for the installation, the package management system, the desktop, and other necessary bits and pieces.

Also: Fedora Everything let me build the Linux desktop I actually want

But more than anything, I always found it best to know which type of distribution should be next.

You wouldn’t want to jump from Ubuntu to, say, Gentoo, as the leap in required skills is considerable. You also wouldn’t want to jump from Ubuntu to Debian, since Ubuntu is based on Debian, making it a lateral move. From my experience, when coming from an Ubuntu-based distribution, the best next distro is one based on Fedora.

This statement wouldn’t hold water five years ago because Fedora often required work to get it running properly. Now, Fedora requires no work or effort to get it working out of the box. Hardware support is on par with Ubuntu, modern boot processes are supported, it has an excellent first-boot experience, Nvidia driver support is out of the box, the touchpad works out of the box, suspend and resume work flawlessly, it ships with a newer kernel, it includes built-in support for modern display stacks, and it’s clean and bloat-free.

Like many Linux distributions, Fedora lets you choose your desktop, but it does so better by offering dedicated spins for each. You’ll find Fedora spins for KDE Plasma, Xfce, Cinnamon, Mate-Compiz, i3, LXQT, LXDE, SOAS, Sway, Budgie, Miracle, Plasma Mobile, and COSMIC. Instead of manually installing your desktop of choice, just download the Fedora spin with your desired desktop.

Also: Fedora 44 made me forget I was using Linux – in the best way

Yes, there’s a Debian-based distribution for every desktop, but knowing you can just go to the Fedora Project Spins page and quickly find what you’re looking for makes the process easy. As well, Ubuntu has its own “flavors” (such as Kubuntu, Lubuntu, etc.), so coming from an Ubuntu flavor will make total sense.

When using a Debian-based distribution, if you install/manage software from the command line, you’re used to APT, such as sudo apt install quillmark. Did you know that Fedora’s DNF works in the same way? That’s right: sudo dnf install quillmark will get you the same results as sudo apt install quillmark (so long as the app is found in the Fedora repositories).

The same holds true for removing software. One difference, however, is that when system software is upgraded, you’ll have to reboot a Fedora-based distribution for the upgrades to take effect. The only time you have to reboot on a Debian-based distro upgrade is if the kernel is upgraded in the process.

If you’re using Ubuntu as your Debian-based distribution, you’ll find that it includes a universal package manager, just as Fedora does. On Debian, the package manager is Snap, while on Fedora it’s Flatpak. While these two are different, they do have some similarities, such as app installation.

Also: 5 of my favorite Linux distros for AI – and why

With Snap packages, the installation goes something like this: sudo snap install quillmark. On Fedora, that command would be flatpak install quillmark. You’ll notice that sudo is not used with Flatpak; the reason for this is that Flatpak apps are typically installed on a per-user basis. Yes, you can install them system-wide, but that defeats the purpose of sandboxing.

Both Fedora and Ubuntu are secure, even if they arrive at that security by different routes. For example, Ubuntu has AppArmor and Fedora has SELinux. However, both of these tools manage Mandatory Access Controls — just in different ways. The good news is that you’ll probably never have to touch either system.

Also: Ubuntu 26.04 vs. Fedora 44: After years of testing both, here’s my verdict

Also, both Debian- and Fedora-based distributions tend to ship with a GUI frontend for the firewall. If you don’t find one installed, you can install one through your package manager. It is important to know that the Fedora firewall manager is considerably more powerful than Ubuntu’s, which also means it has a steeper learning curve. The good news is that, out of the box, you probably won’t have to make many changes to the firewall, other than ensuring it’s enabled.

Once upon a time, I would have debated such a statement, but Fedora is now on par with Ubuntu in terms of user-friendliness, especially if you choose one of the more user-friendly spins (such as KDE Fedora, Cinnamon, or MATE-Compiz). Fedora also has a System Settings app similar to Ubuntu’s; each one lets you manage nearly every aspect of the computer, so there’s no need to use the command line with Fedora (unless you want to).

With Debian, the release cycle is every 2 years, and support is 5 years. With Fedora, the release cycle is every 6 months, and support is 13 months. If you’re using an Ubuntu-based distribution (which is based on Debian), the release cycle is the same as Fedora, but there are two versions: LTS and interim. LTS support is considerably longer than interim releases: LTS releases receive 5 years of free support, while interim releases receive 9 months.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me

In the end, the Fedora release/support cycle is faster and simpler.

Because both development teams focus on building a user-friendly distribution out of the box, migrating from a Debian-based to a Fedora-based distribution is seamless. When making such a transition, aside from a few minor differences, you’ll feel like you never left your Debian-based distro, especially if you choose a Fedora Spin that includes the same desktop you’ve been using.

Quadruped rainbows target multiple muscle groups efficiently

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Most of us don’t have hours to devote to working out, so when there’s an exercise that can strengthen multiple muscle groups at the same time, I’m quick to use with my personal training clients.

Quadruped rainbows are one such exercise. This no-equipment move targets the glutes, hamstrings, hips, deep core, and even the shoulder stabilizing muscles, making it a great option when time is limited. The standard version is appropriate for beginners, but there are plenty of ways to up the challenge level if you’re more advanced.

Roll out your yoga mat and give quadruped rainbows a try during your next workout.

Before trying any new exercise, be sure to check in with your doctor first. They may recommend avoiding certain movements based on your health background.

Beginners should consider working with a certified personal trainer to learn how to do quadruped rainbows properly. A trainer can also provide modifications if needed and progression options when you’re ready. Doing any exercise with poor form can lead to pain or injury.

Aside from a yoga mat, those with sore knees may want to use a pillow or a rolled-up towel for additional cushioning.

Start with one set of 10 reps on each side. Gradually increase your reps to 12 on each side and add an additional set. Eventually, you’ll aim for 3 sets of 15 reps on each side.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Do quadruped rainbows 2-3 times a week at first, then work your way up to 3-4 times per week. The exercise can be done on its own, as a part of another workout, or as a warm-up for more intense exercise.

You should feel muscle fatigue but never sharp pain when doing this exercise. Stop the exercise and consult your physician if you feel sharp pain at any point.

This exercise works the glutes, hip abductors, hip adductors, hamstrings, deep core muscles like the rectus abdominis and internal obliques, and rotator cuff muscles.

The arc-like movement of the leg promotes optimal hip mobility and range of motion. In the quadruped position, your deep core works to stabilize your entire body as the active leg moves into each position.

Additionally, quadruped rainbows don’t require any equipment and are accessible for a wide range of fitness levels and abilities.

If you’ve just started to work out regularly, you may find it difficult to keep proper form during this exercise. The biggest form compensations I see are rotating the hips side to side as you move the leg back and forth, excessive arching in the lower back, and sinking the chest towards the floor.

If you notice any of these compensations, it may indicate some deep core weakness. In addition to including exercises like diaphragmatic breathing, planks, and hollow holds in your routine, you may also want to modify the quadruped rainbow.

Instead of sweeping your leg to the side in a semi-circular motion, try simply lifting the active leg. Aim to bring the knee and ankle in line with the hips. Hold briefly, and then lower the toe back towards the floor.

You can also practice donkey kicks in preparation for the standard quadruped rainbow. Keep the active leg bent at a 90-degree angle, then kick the heel towards the ceiling. Pause briefly, then lower the active leg back to the starting position.

As you get stronger and more conditioned, quadruped rainbows may not challenge you like it did at first. The easiest way to increase the challenge is to add reps and sets.

That being said, sometimes doing more than 15 reps of an exercise can get rather monotonous. Wearing ankle weights is another easy way to up the ante, as is performing the exercise on an unstable surface like a balance pad or Bosu ball. Just be sure your form stays solid throughout the exercise.
